policies.name: About the Institute
policies.purpose: Identity, vision, mission, objectives and quality policy of the institute.

provisions.text: K. J. Somaiya Institute of Engineering and Information Technology (KJSIEIT) was established by the Somaiya Trust in the year 2001 at the Ayurvihar campus, Sion, Mumbai 400 022.
The College is housed in a G+8 storey building with airy classrooms, hi-tech laboratories, auditorium, canteen and common rooms.

The institute is adjacent to the Eastern Express Highway. Chunabhatti and Sion are the nearest railway stations on the Harbour line and Central line respectively; the nearest bus stop is Everard Nagar, Chunabhatti on Eastern Highway.

Vision: To be universally accepted as a synonym of quality, excellence and commitment in the field of engineering education by nurturing talent and transforming young minds to realize their potential and become future ready engineers.

Mission: (1) provide students a thorough knowledge of engineering to refine their professional skills; (2) nurture creativity and innovation while encouraging multidisciplinary interaction; (3) train students to be industry ready and effective individually and in a team; (4) inculcate ethical behavior, responsibility and commitment.

Quality Policy: conform to the requirements of AICTE, DTE and University of Mumbai; maintain transparency and fair practices in admission and recruitment; ensure continuous evaluation and examination; provide high-end laboratory, computing and smart-classroom resources; ensure a safe and secure environment for all stakeholders; promote industry-institute interaction, R&D, placements and co/extra-curricular activities.

policies.name: Governance and Statutory Bodies
policies.purpose: Constitution, term, meeting frequency and functions of the four statutory bodies of the autonomous institute.
policies.scope: KJSIEIT as an Autonomous Institute, following UGC guidelines per UGC Notification dated 12 February 2018.

provisions.text: KJSIEIT, being an Autonomous Institute, follows governance as per the prescribed guidelines of the University Grants Commission, per UGC Notification dated 12 February 2018.

Governing Body composition: 5 members from the Management/Trust (with the Chairman or President/Director as chairperson), 2 teachers of the College nominated by the Principal by seniority by rotation, 1 educationist or industrialist nominated by the management, 1 UGC nominee, 1 State Government nominee (academician not below the rank of professor, or a State Government official of the Directorate of Higher Education / State Council of Higher Education), 1 University nominee, and the Principal ex-officio.

The Governing Body guides the college in fulfilling the objectives for which autonomous status was granted; institutes scholarships, fellowships, studentships, medals, prizes and certificates on the recommendation of the Academic Council; approves new programs of study leading to degrees and/or diplomas; makes all recruitments of Teaching Faculty and Principal in accordance with UGC and State Government policies; and approves the annual budget of the college before submission to the UGC.

Academic Council composition: the Principal (Chairman); all Heads of Departments; four teachers of the college representing different categories of teaching staff by rotation on seniority; not less than four experts/academicians from outside the college nominated by the Governing Body; three University nominees not below Professor; and one faculty member nominated by the Principal as Member Secretary.
The term of nominated members of the Academic Council is three years, and the Academic Council shall meet at least twice a year.

The Academic Council scrutinizes and approves Board of Studies proposals on courses of study, academic regulations, curricula, syllabi, instructional and evaluation arrangements; makes regulations on admission of students; makes regulations for sports, extra-curricular activities and maintenance of playgrounds and hostels; and recommends new programs and scholarships to the Governing Body. Where it differs on a proposal it may return the matter to the Board of Studies or reject it, giving reasons.

Board of Studies composition: the Head of the Department concerned (Chairman); the entire faculty of each specialization; two subject experts from outside the Parent University nominated by the Academic Council; one expert nominated by the Vice-Chancellor from a panel of six recommended by the Principal; one representative from industry/corporate sector/allied area relating to placement; and one postgraduate meritorious alumnus nominated by the Principal.
The term of nominated Board of Studies members is three years and the Board of Studies shall meet at least twice a year.

The Board of Studies prepares syllabi for various courses for approval of the Academic Council, suggests methodologies for innovative teaching and evaluation, suggests a panel of names to the Academic Council for appointment of examiners, and coordinates research, teaching, extension and other academic activities.

Finance Committee composition: the Principal (Chairman); one person nominated by the Governing Body for two years; the Finance Officer of the affiliating University; and one senior-most teacher of the college nominated in rotation by the Principal for two years. Its term is three years and it meets at least twice a year. It acts as an advisory body to the Governing Body on budget estimates and audited accounts.

policies.name: Admission Process
policies.purpose: To have better quality students as input to KJSIEIT in a transparent manner.
policies.scope: First Year, Direct Second Year and postgraduate admissions, governed by DTE, MHT-CET Cell, Pravesh Niyantran Samiti, AICTE and University of Mumbai guidelines.

provisions.text: An Admission Committee headed by a senior faculty or administrative person coordinates all admission-related activities, develops and reviews the application form, admission brochures and admission process, and draws up the schedule for advertisements, brochures, receiving forms, merit lists and admission rounds.

To get better quality students, all Minority Seats and Institute Level Seats are surrendered to the Centralized Admission Process (CAP) conducted by the competent authority. Students are admitted as per the allotment of seats by the competent authority in CAP rounds.

Admission for CAP and CAP-MI (Minority) seats: (1) the competent authority allots the candidate a seat in a branch; (2) the candidate visits the college website; (3) reads the e-brochure; (4) registers on the college website, fills the Online Pre-admission Form and takes a printout; (5) comes to college with the printed admission form, required documents and fees.

For CAP Vacancy seats the candidate additionally submits the printed admission form with documents and processing fees at the college office after verification; provisional merit lists are displayed on the college website and notice board; time is given for grievances; final corrected merit lists are displayed with the admission schedule; and candidates are called for counselling rounds by merit number.

At the time of admission, original documents such as mark sheet, leaving certificate and caste certificate are collected as per the type of candidate. All candidates must submit a medical fitness certificate. For minority candidates a domicile certificate of Maharashtra state is compulsory.

At admission the candidate pays, in the accounts department, tuition fees and development fees as decided by Shikshan Shulka Samiti; University fees (insurance, e-facility, disaster relief fund, enrolment fees, Amartya Shiksha Yojana, Vice Chancellor's Fund, student welfare fund etc.); and examination fees.
The candidate fills the enrolment form and eligibility form in the student section, and fills the online anti-ragging affidavit.

The admission process is completed on the cut-off date mentioned by DTE in the admission notification. Details of all students are forwarded to the Jt. DTE office, DTE office and Pravesh Niyantran Samiti for approval.

policies.name: Induction of Students
policies.purpose: Provide basic information to new students entering an unfamiliar environment on the first day of college.

provisions.text: On the first day of college an induction program (Orientation Course) is conducted which provides basic information to students.

The induction program covers: introducing the college; explaining the roles of teachers and students; introducing the Principal, HODs and teachers and where they are available; introducing first-year subjects and labs with their locations; introducing the library, sports section and other facilities; the organization structure; the examination scheme; the academic calendar; general rules and regulations regarding attendance; the Student-Teacher mentoring system; the code of conduct; the Anti-Ragging Committee and discipline committee members; University enrollment and examination forms; available scholarships; student chapters such as IEEE, ISTE, IETE, CSI and IET; Training and Placement activity; and a Fresher's Party.

policies.name: Programs and Departments
policies.purpose: Vision, mission, Program Educational Objectives, Program Outcomes and Program Specific Objectives of every department, and the departmental governance bodies.

provisions.text: KJSIEIT has departments of Electronics and Telecommunication Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Computer Engineering, Information Technology, Artificial Intelligence and Data Science, and Basic Sciences and Humanities, plus the postgraduate M.Tech in Artificial Intelligence.

provisions.section: 2.1 Department of Electronics and Telecommunication Engineering
provisions.text: The Electronics and Telecommunication Engineering department started in 2001 with an intake of 60. In 2003 the intake increased to 120 and continues to remain the same.

provisions.section: 2.5 Department of Artificial Intelligence and Data Science
provisions.text: The Artificial Intelligence and Data Science undergraduate engineering course was started by the institute from the academic year July 2020 with an intake capacity of 60 seats.

A Department Advisory Board (DAB) is constituted for each department consisting of the Head of the Department, industry representatives, a parent representative, an alumni representative and two senior faculty members. It meets before the commencement of every semester and acts as the primary source of external guidance for the department.

The Departmental Quality Circle (DQC) meeting is held before the beginning of each semester. DQC is headed by the Head of the Department with 5-6 teachers as members, finalises the departmental academic calendar and ensures timely, efficient and progressive performance of academic tasks.

The Program Assessment Committee (PAC) is formed under the leadership of the Head of the Department, with one senior faculty as academic coordinator and class-teachers as members. It monitors and evaluates programme delivery and prepares periodic progress reports; monthly monitoring reports on syllabus completion are collected and corrective actions devised in HOD meetings.

policies.name: M.Tech in Artificial Intelligence - Programme Rules
policies.purpose: Eligibility, intake, duration and structure of the postgraduate M.Tech in Artificial Intelligence.

provisions.text: Master of Technology in Artificial Intelligence: discipline Computer Engineering, intake 18 seats, duration 2 years.

Eligibility for M.Tech in Artificial Intelligence: passed Bachelor Degree in Computer Engineering / Information Technology / Electrical Engineering / Electronics Engineering / Electronics and Telecommunication Engineering / Instrumentation Engineering / Power Electronics with at least 50% marks (at least 45% marks for candidates of Backward class categories, Economically Weaker Section (EWS) and persons with disability belonging to Maharashtra State).

numbers.of: minimum marks for backward class, EWS and PwD candidates of Maharashtra

provisions.text: Requisite for M.Tech in AI: a non-zero positive GATE score in Computer Science and Information Technology (CS), Electronics and Communication Engineering (EC), Electrical Engineering (EE) or Instrumentation Engineering (IN) streams, OR full-time work experience of 2 years with a sponsorship certificate from the employer.

Courses offered in M.Tech AI: Machine Learning and Pattern Recognition, Mathematical Foundations of Data Science, Deep and Reinforcement Learning, Natural Language Processing, Robotics Process Automation, Bio-inspired AI, Big Data Analytics, Information Retrieval, AI in Bio-informatics, Autonomous Robotics, Computer Vision, IoT Data Analytics, Speech Recognition, Blockchain and Mixed Reality.

Salient features cited: more than 40 research grants received, more than 35 MoUs signed with industries, a Center of Excellence in Robotics Process Automation, and 24x7 access to IEEE, ACM, Elsevier and Springer digital libraries.

policies.name: Accounts Section Policy
policies.purpose: To provide the accounting officer with direction and guidance on accounting transactions, procedures and reports.

provisions.text: The Institute followed the cash system of accounting up to 31 March 2004 and shifted to the Mercantile system effective 1 April 2004. Accounting is fully automated; ERP Tally 9/4.91 was used from 2007 and the Institute currently uses Net Suite Oracle based software.
To claim full tax exemption an educational institution has to apply at least 85% of its income for the purpose for which the trust has been set up; adequate records are maintained for tax compliance.

numbers.of: minimum income applied to trust purpose

provisions.text: Cash balance allowed at any point of time is Rs. 20,000 for petty cash expenses. An imprest is maintained so that cash in hand never falls below Rs. 5,000.

Bank account opening is authorized by the Hon. Secretary, Somaiya Vidyavihar. The designated signatories for operating bank accounts are the Hon. Secretary Somaiya Vidyavihar, the Principal and other authorized members passed by the Governing Body. Disbursements are authorized by the Hon. Secretary; operational disbursements by the Principal / Registrar.
If a cheque is not encashed within the mandatory period of three months the recipient is credited again and the claim is settled on demand.

Salary will be paid on or before the 10th of the succeeding month. Any error or miscalculation is to be brought to the Accountant and after due verification will be released by the 15th or adjusted in the following month.

Staff members must furnish investment details by 30 June for TDS calculation, and submit proof of investment (photocopy) to the Accounts Section on or before 20 December. If not done, TDS will be fully deducted and no grievance, complaint or request will be entertained.

Staff must submit their PAN to the Accounts Section at the time of joining. Salary is disbursed through bank, for which staff are required to open a salary account with Axis Bank, Ghatkopar Branch Mumbai.

No staff or students are permitted to collect money, fees or anything similar. Only Accounts staff duly authorized by the Principal and Registrar may collect money, fees or fines. The Librarian is authorized to collect fines from students and staff, and the amount is deposited with the Accounts Department at the earliest. Only the Accounts department is authorized to disburse payments approved by the competent authority.

Teaching and non-teaching staff appointed as regular employees are eligible for an annual increment as prescribed by rule, subject to performance appraisal and ACR. Staff who availed Leave Without Pay (LWP) beyond 15 days will not be eligible for the annual increment.

numbers.of: LWP threshold that forfeits annual increment

provisions.text: All HODs and in-charges work out their department's requirement for the next financial year as per Accounts Section guidelines and give it to the Accountant per the circular in December. The budget is presented to the Management and after approval is communicated to HODs by April.

All cash transactions during the month of March are to be settled by 28 March to enable the accounts department to close the accounts for the financial year. Staff must settle expenses by the end of every month; expenses are not carried to the following month.

Depreciation on fixed assets is provided on the straight line method at rates prescribed by Shikshan Shulka Samiti / Fees Regulating Authority: Building 2.5%; Furniture and Fixtures 10%; Library books included in teaching 25%; Office Equipment 40%; Lab Equipments 10%; Computers Equipment and software 40%; Air Conditioning Equipments 10.
provisions.ambiguity: The Air Conditioning Equipments rate is printed as '10' with no percent sign in the source table.

provisions.section: 5.1.9 Day to Day in Accounts Section item 5-6
provisions.text: Passbook and cheque book verification against the bank statement is done twice a year and verified by a Chartered Accountant. Internal Audit is conducted quarterly and External Audit twice a year.

The loan process is approved in a Governing Body meeting; after approval the institute applies to the Charity Commissioner, submitting a resolution, the purpose of the loan and the nature of repayment. A 5-6 year budget is projected and the loan applied for to the bank as per bank norms. On sanction with a repayment schedule, the required documents are registered at the Registrar office, Govt. of Maharashtra.

policies.name: Fee Collection Policy
policies.purpose: How tuition fees are determined, paid and followed up.

provisions.text: Fees are collected from students as per the college Fee policy recommended by Shikshan Shulka Samiti / Fees Regulating Authority and the University of Mumbai.

Before paying the fees a student should fill the online admission form on the college website, take a printout of the admission form, attach a photocopy of the marksheet and get it verified from the Student Section.
Tuition fees are collected online through the My Account Portal only. Computerized fee receipts are issued to students through the online student portal only.
After a particular period, students who have not paid the fees are reminded through a circular and their names are sent to the HODs of their respective departments.
provisions.ambiguity: 'After a particular period' is not quantified in the source.

provisions.text: If a student has a financial problem, a time extension is given to the student after consulting with the Principal.

provisions.topic: where to find the fee structure
provisions.text: The fee structure is made available on the college website under the Admission menu.

NOT SPECIFIED IN SOURCE: no fee refund, cancellation or withdrawal policy appears anywhere in the Institute Policy Handbook. Section 5.1.7 covers only how fees are determined and collected. The only refund-adjacent rule in the whole corpus is that the Rs. 500 provisional-admission fee charged pending revaluation is not refunded if the revaluation fails.
provisions.ambiguity: A student leaving or cancelling admission mid-year cannot be told what, if anything, is refundable. The governing rules would be those of the Fees Regulating Authority / Shikshan Shulka Samiti, which this handbook references but does not reproduce.

policies.purpose: How the Student Section handles admission records and issues certificates to students.

provisions.text: A leaving certificate is issued to a student leaving the college. The application is available on the institute website. Before issuing the leaving certificate, a no dues certificate signed by the respective HODs is collected from the student. The leaving certificate is issued within 3-5 days after receiving the application.

provisions.text: A bonafide certificate is issued to a student on application; the form is available on the institute website. The purpose for issuing it is specifically mentioned in the certificate. The bonafide certificate is issued within one day after receiving the application.

A migration certificate is issued to passed-out students. The student fills the migration form available on the University of Mumbai website; the duly filled form with required documents is accepted by the Student Section, which submits it to the Eligibility & Migration Department, University of Mumbai. The migration certificate is collected from the University within 10-15 days.

provisions.text: During First Year, Direct Second Year and Master of Engineering admission, required documents are collected from students and maintained in separate files. Student information is uploaded on the DTE and CET Cell website. After the admission process, merit lists with required documents are submitted to the Joint Director of Technical Education (Jt. DTE) and the Admission Regulating Authority (ARA) for approval.

Newly admitted students fill the enrolment form available on the University website; printed copies are collected and submitted to the University of Mumbai for confirmation of enrolment. Newly admitted students also submit the online anti-ragging affidavit available on the AICTE website, and a printout is collected and maintained.

For Second Year, Third Year, Final Year and Master of Engineering, the notification for admission is issued after the declaration of result. Admission forms of the students are verified and collected.

policies.name: Scholarship and Freeship Schemes
policies.purpose: Government, trust and institute scholarship and freeship schemes available to students and how to apply.

provisions.text: E.B.C. Concession is a State Government scholarship scheme for students domiciled in Maharashtra, admitted under CAP, whose family income is below Rs. 8.0 lacs. Students claiming Economically Backward Class concession must produce an Income Certificate issued by the Executive Magistrate at the time of admission, and apply online on the MahaDBT portal. The Student Section scrutinises the application and sends it for approval to the Competent Authority.

numbers.of: maximum family income for EBC concession

provisions.text: Concession in Fees for Backward Class Category Candidates (Maharashtra State only) covers SC, ST, VJDTNT(A), NT(B), NT(C), NT(D), SBC and OBC candidates admitted under CAP holding a Caste Certificate and Caste Validity of Maharashtra State. Students receive only the amount of waiver notified in circulars issued by the Social Justice and Tribal Welfare Departments from time to time, subject to their norms. Application is online on the MahaDBT portal.

The Minorities Development Department, Government of Maharashtra offers a Merit Cum Means Scholarship of maximum Rs. 25,000 for economically weaker and meritorious students belonging to Muslim, Sikh, Buddhist, Christian, Parsi, Jain and Jews minority communities pursuing professional and technical education. Eligible students apply online on the MahaDBT Portal.

Central Government schemes include (a) Merit cum Means Based Scholarship (MCM) for economically weaker and meritorious minority students, (b) J&K PMSSS Scholarship for J&K students, and (c) PMSSS - Central Armed Force & Assam Rifle. Students under (a) and (c) apply on the NSP Portal; J&K PMSSS students apply on the aicte-pmsss portal.

KJSIEIT Merit Cum Means Scholarship / Sponsorship gives a 50% concession in tuition fee to 11 First Year students: Computer Engineering 1, Information Technology 1, Electronics & Telecommunication 6, Electronics Engineering 3. The candidate should be economically weak but deserving with an excellent academic record, with yearly income not more than Rs. 2,00,000, and must submit an income certificate from the appropriate authority. The minimum cut-off marks are decided at the time of the admission process.

The KJSIEIT Merit Cum Means Scholarship/Sponsorship of a student will be discontinued without any notice if the student is found indulging in anti-institutional activities, ragging, or any other activity contrary to rules of discipline. It will also be discontinued if the candidate's yearly progress report is not satisfactory.
The Somaiya Women Scholarship is open to all Somaiya Vidyavihar / Somaiya Ayurvihar women students with a financial need and a good educational track record.
The Somaiya Need Based Scholarship is open to all Somaiya Vidyavihar / Somaiya Ayurvihar students with a financial need and a good educational track record.

provisions.topic: how to apply for a scholarship
provisions.text: Circulars and notifications for all scholarships are available on the Institute Website. Students fill the online or offline form as per the circular or the portal of the respective scholarship and submit it to the Student Section with the necessary documents. The Student Section verifies the form and documents and sends them to the competent authority for approval. After approval, the Accounts Section receives the scholarship payment by NEFT or Demand Draft and disburses it to the student as per rule, and prepares the Utilization Certificate after disbursing the payment.

policies.name: Student Insurance Schemes
policies.purpose: The mandatory and University group insurance cover available to students.

provisions.text: Amartya Insurance was implemented by the Government of Maharashtra and DTE for Degree Courses in Engineering/Technology across Maharashtra vide G.R. No. TEM-2011/(11/2011) TECH EU 04 dated 25 August 2011. The scheme is mandatory for all colleges and students to pay and get insured from Academic Year 2012-2013. The Student Section collects student data in the insurer's format and sends the proposal for insurance cover of the student and the earning member of the student.

Amartya Insurance risk cover: death, if the injury within twelve calendar months of its occurrence is the sole and direct cause of death of the insured parent/legal guardian; permanent total disablement within twelve calendar months; and loss of two limbs or two eyes or one limb and one eye within twelve calendar months of occurrence.

Yuva Raksha is a group insurance scheme introduced by the University of Mumbai from Academic Year 2002-2003 for students of affiliated colleges. It covers accidental death (rail/road/air accidents, violent collision, fall injury due to fire, explosion, snakebite, frostbite, burn injury, drowning, poisoning, natural calamity and riots) but excludes suicide or attempted suicide. The policy provides 100% coverage on death of the insured, 100% coverage for permanent disability (loss of limbs, eyesight, hearing or paralysis) and 100% coverage for hospitalization expenses arising out of accidents including medicines and doctor fees.

numbers.of: coverage on death, permanent disability and accident hospitalization

policies.name: Railway Concession
policies.purpose: Rail travel concession available to students and the process for obtaining it.

provisions.text: Free railway concession forms are issued to girl students who want to avail the facility in second class. A 70% concession in pass is given to SC category students. A 40% concession in pass is given to boys for second class and first class. Concession is also given to students going for an Industrial Visit and to their native place during the vacation period. Around 80% of students avail this facility.

numbers.of: concession for boys, second and first class
share of students availing the facility

provisions.text: Since April 2017 students apply online for the pass. The student applies on the online concession form; the concession-issuing staff verifies the form against date of birth, validity of the previously issued concession, residential proof, form number, pass number, date of issue, caste, source and destination; and concession is given for the nearest station within two working days. The completed concession form book with statement is submitted to the Railway Section, CST, which after verification gives an acknowledgement slip and issues a new concession book.

policies.name: Hostel Facility
policies.purpose: Availability, eligibility, allotment and timing rules of hostel accommodation for KJSIEIT students.

provisions.text: KJSIEIT has hostel facility of the Somaiya Trust for Somaiya students only. Every year the Institute receives a number of seats from three hostels - Somaiya Polytechnic Hostel, Somaiya Management Institute Hostel and Somaiya Medical Hostel - of the Vidyavihar and Ayurvihar campuses.

After taking admission in the Institute the aspirant submits a request letter to the Student Section for the hostel. The application is forwarded to the Office Superintendent. As per the student's need, students who are non-residents of Mumbai and the suburbs of the Mumbai region can be eligible for the hostel. The final shortlisted students are allotted rooms as per availability of seats in any of the three Somaiya Vidyavihar hostels.
Fees and mess charges can be paid by the student for the semester as prescribed by the concerned hostel authorities.
provisions.ambiguity: The handbook does not state hostel fee or mess charge amounts; they are set by each hostel authority.

provisions.text: Timing of hostel is from 9.00 am to 8.00 pm to enter. Rectors are residents in the hostel who manage basic requirements of the students and maintain discipline in the hostel.

For students taking hostel admission, the Principal and officers assigned by the Principal act as guardians of the admitted students. The appointed officer coordinates between the hostel authorities and the Principal for necessary requirements of students.

policies.name: Stores and Purchase Policy
policies.purpose: Institute-level purchase procedure, quotation and negotiation rules, and annual stock verification.

provisions.text: As per indents or requisitions made by departments, quotations from a minimum of three parties and a maximum of five parties are invited and analyzed by preparing a comparative statement. A negotiation meeting is then held in the presence of the Principal / Vice-Principal, the Purchase department representative of Management, the Purchase department representative of the Institute, the Project office representative of the management and the accountant.
Out of all quotations received, the vendor quoting least or providing quality material is issued a Work / Purchase order of the Institute as per the negotiation meeting.

All consumable, non-consumable and capital purchase bills are processed for billing to the Accounts Section through the Store & Purchase Section. Billing is carried out by the Accounts Section within three working days.

Computers should be replaced after every five years. Old furniture and paper scrap should be disposed of every year with the consent of the Office Superintendent and HOD as per the Principal / Vice-Principal's instructions.
provisions.ambiguity: CONTRADICTS sections 3.2.6 and 5.4.4 of the same handbook, both of which state computers should be replaced after every seven years. REQUIRES VERIFICATION.

provisions.text: All HODs and in-charges are required to conduct stock verification every year in December / January and submit the statement and certificate to the Stores in-charge and Office Superintendent. Stock of a department is verified by a member of the stock verification committee from another department.

All AMC for maintaining infrastructure is done with the proper procedure. The Store and Purchase section initiates the process with the guidance of the Office Superintendent and instructions of the Principal / Vice-Principal, calls three or more quotations from the concerned parties, and the least quoted party is finalized to give the AMC with the consent of the Project team of Management, the Purchase team of Management and the Principal / Vice-Principal.

policies.name: Maintenance Section and Rental Policy
policies.purpose: Upkeep of inside and outside infrastructure, equipment maintenance, scrap disposal, and the rates at which institute premises are rented out.

provisions.text: For inside cleaning (classrooms, auditorium, washrooms) an Annual Maintenance Contract is given to a private agency and cleaning is done daily. Small-scale furniture repair is carried out with the help of Workshop staff. AC and water cooler maintenance is contracted to the sister concern K. J. Somaiya Vocational Training Institute, Vidyavihar. An external agency is appointed for aqua-guard maintenance and periodic cleaning of water tanks.

For outside maintenance and cleaning (playground, garden) an Annual Maintenance Contract is given to a private agency. Grass cutting is done periodically, security staff is appointed for security and trespassing issues, and solar panels mounted on the pathways are cleaned every month.

Maintenance cards are maintained for every equipment. Lab assistants maintain lab equipment regularly, equipment is calibrated on a regular basis, and every maintenance activity is recorded in the maintenance card.

Non-working equipment which is not repairable should be disposed of with the consent of the HOD and Principal. Computers should be replaced after every seven years. Old furniture and scrap paper should be disposed of every year with the consent of the HOD and Principal. Scrap is disposed either by selling to vendors or, for electronic scrap, by giving it to recycling institutions.
provisions.ambiguity: CONTRADICTS section 5.5.1 item 10 of the same handbook, which states five years. REQUIRES VERIFICATION.

provisions.text: As per the institute's purchase policy, for purchasing IT equipment the preferable warranty period is 5-5-5 years (5 years onsite warranty with service and spare) for desktop and laptop computers, and 3-3-3 years for servers followed by AMC. For printers and other equipment the warranty period is generally one year, after which repair and maintenance is on a call basis.

The IT centre team decides the life period of IT equipment considering Govt./University e-scrap guidelines: desktop computers 7 years, servers 7 years, laptop computers 5 years, printers 7 years, network switches 10 years, surveillance cameras 10 years.

numbers.of: network switch and surveillance camera life

provisions.text: E-scrap procedure: a history card is maintained for each equipment and verified before scrapping; the department lists equipment to be scrapped; IT coordinators verify equipment history and status; the Scrap Committee (all heads, Office Superintendent, Store & Purchase section in-charge and the IT team) prepares a report; the report goes to the Office Superintendent and Principal for scrap approval and then to the data centre SVV (IT manager); on approval the equipment is handed to the store department; data centre SVV sends a team from K. J. Somaiya Private I.T.I., Vidyavihar to extract usable equipment for other Somaiya institutes as a policy of Somaiya Trust; usable equipment is transferred to those institutes; the store department calls quotations from government-authorized vendors for e-scrap; after scrapping, the equipment is marked 'Scrapped' in dead stock registers and recorded in the books of accounts.

Rental rates finalized according to Somaiya Vidyavihar guidelines: Classroom Rs. 4,000 per day; Auditorium without AC Rs. 35,000 per day; Auditorium with AC Rs. 60,000 per day; College Ground Rs. 55,000 per day; Playground Big for outsiders Rs. 20,000 per day; Playground Big free for Somaiya students and for University / DSO; Astro Turf Football ground for Somaiya students Rs. 600 per hour (6.00 am to 7.00 pm) or Rs. 750 (6.00 am to midnight); Astro Turf Football ground for outsiders Rs. 1,300 per hour (6.00 am to 7.00 pm) or Rs. 1,500 per hour (6.00 am to midnight).
On Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays the rates applicable to outsiders will be applicable to Somaiya students too.

policies.name: Teaching Learning Process
policies.purpose: Framework enabling teachers to ensure all students experience an excellent ambiance for learning and teaching.

provisions.text: At KJSIEIT students are the first priority: 'The Institute is fully committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of our students. They are the focal point of all our planning, delivery, evaluation and continuous improvement.' The Institute firmly believes all students have the potential to succeed and should be empowered to realize their potential.

The Institute adheres to the curriculum prescribed by the University of Mumbai (UoM) and has a well laid out plan to implement it. The Principal, Dean Academics, HODs and the Internal Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC) develop and deploy action plans as per suggestions and guidelines from the Governing Body and Departmental Advisory Boards.
provisions.ambiguity: AMBIGUOUS / REQUIRES VERIFICATION. This 2022 chapter describes the institute as following the University of Mumbai curriculum, while the 2022 Examination Policy chapter and the current Exam Cell data describe KJSIT as an autonomous institute running its own CBCGS scheme approved by its own Academic Council. The two chapters of the same handbook edition are not consistent on this point.

provisions.text: Planning for the next semester is done at the end of the current semester by taking subject choices from each faculty, considering choices, competency and area of expertise. Rotation of subjects is done as per requirement; generally a subject is allotted to a faculty for at least three years to ensure quality teaching.

The institutional academic calendar and departmental academic calendars are prepared in alignment with the University calendar and displayed on the Institute website and departmental notice boards prior to the commencement of the next semester.

Departmental time-tables are prepared by mutual consultation of all departmental time table co-ordinators under the guidance of the Dean Academics and the central time table co-ordinator. Based on the academic calendar and time-table each faculty prepares a date-wise Teaching Plan and Lab Plan, verified by the Academic Committee and approved by the HOD. Faculty also maintain a detailed course file / academic diary.
At the end of every month, Academic Committee members of the respective department collect data from each faculty about completion of syllabus and conduction and compensation of lectures.

Two tests are conducted as per the dates mentioned in the Academic Calendar. The average of both tests is considered for passing marks. Based on Term Test 1 marks the department identifies weak students per subject.
provisions.ambiguity: AMBIGUOUS. This chapter says the AVERAGE of both tests is considered; the current Exam Cell data states that for B.Tech Scheme III the TOTAL of both tests is considered (average only for M.Tech Scheme II). REQUIRES VERIFICATION against the scheme in force for the student's batch.

provisions.text: In addition to regular lectures, remedial lectures, revision lectures and doubt-solving sessions are arranged for the academic improvement of students.
Teacher feedback from students on the teaching-learning process is taken twice a semester and analysed by the HOD for improving teaching quality.
The attendance list of students is displayed on the notice board at the end of every month. The same information is communicated to parents through letters/emails, SMS and phone calls.

Parent-Teacher meetings are conducted twice a semester, keeping parents updated about their ward's progress and departmental and institute activities. Parents' feedback and suggestions are collected at the PTM and steps are taken to comply with them.
An external academic audit is conducted towards the end of the semester.

policies.name: Laboratory Policy
policies.purpose: Objectives of laboratory instruction, responsibilities of lab staff and faculty, rules for students, purchasing, disposal and safety.

provisions.text: A student's batch should consist of 15 to 20 students. In computer labs one student must get one computer to work on.

For each laboratory one Laboratory In charge is appointed, responsible for maintaining the Dead Stock and Consumable Registers with the lab assistant; procuring consumables before the start of every academic year; displaying the lab time table, names of lab in charge and lab assistant, experiment list and equipment list on the lab notice board; planning equipment procurement in advance; ensuring adequate infrastructure so each batch can complete practicals; organizing the lab for oral and practical examinations; recovering costs for any breakage or loss; ensuring cleanliness and switching off equipment after use; submitting consumable requisitions to the HOD who verifies and forwards them to the Principal; and reporting loss or theft to the HOD in writing.

The Lab Assistant prepares laboratories for smooth conduction of sessions; maintains dead stock, consumable and maintenance registers; numbers every new instrument/equipment; gets non-working equipment or computers repaired and records it in the equipment maintenance card; installs new equipment and maintains existing equipment; installs software needed for lab sessions; maintains and updates the approved supplier list; and gets equipment calibrated regularly.

Faculty conducting practicals or projects are responsible for the respective labs during their practical hours, must provide the lab manual of their subject to students, and shall follow the guidelines prepared by the Lab in-charge; faculty may suggest changes with the consent of the HOD.

Lab rules for students: the ID card is compulsory while entering the lab; switch off the mobile phone before entering; keep bags on the rack; carry journal papers during the practical session; do not move equipment between tables without permission; complete write-ups once a practical is performed; maintain silence and do not sit idle; do not play with instruments or equipment; during practical sessions other students are not allowed in the lab; switch off the mains supply after the practical; return components, breadboards and experimental kits to the lab assistant; keep stools in their places before leaving; read the lab notice board regularly; keep the supply off while making or removing connections and get connections checked by the subject teacher before switching on; do not remove ICs from kits; switch off equipment not in use; report breakages; do not perform unauthorized experiments; and do not leave an on-going experiment unattended.
A fine will be charged on all the students for any damage done to the instruments by any student.
provisions.ambiguity: The fine amount is NOT SPECIFIED IN SOURCE.

provisions.text: Lab purchasing: (1) the lab in-charge raises a requisition (indent) in the prescribed indent form and submits it to the Head of Department for scrutiny; (2) the HOD submits the indent to the store section; (3) the Stores Section forwards the indent to the Registrar and submits it to the Principal for final approval; (4) after approval the Stores Section is intimated for quotations; (5) after sanction by the Principal the order is placed; (6) on receipt the lab in-charge certifies quality and forwards the bill to the Store Section, which forwards it to Accounts for payment after signatures of Registrar and Principal; (7) the Store Section numbers capital items and records the location in the stock register; (8) the original bill is kept with Accounts and photocopies with Stores/HODs; (9) purchase is strictly as per Head Office guidelines.
Non-working equipment which is not repairable should be disposed of with the consent of the HOD and Principal. Computers should be replaced after every seven years.
provisions.ambiguity: CONTRADICTS section 5.5.1 item 10 of the same handbook edition, which states five years.

provisions.text: Computer lab rules: no personal information should be stored on the computer; files and folders should be well organized and junk information cleaned regularly; antivirus should be installed; computers should be formatted and the OS reinstalled at regular intervals; a record of installed software should be maintained; the number of prints per printer should be noted with the date of cartridge change or refill; and renewal of licenses or warranty should be monitored.

Safety guidelines: examine all electrical cords periodically for wear and damage and unplug and repair damaged cords; properly ground all electrical equipment; if sparks are noticed while plugging or unplugging or if the cord feels hot, do not use the equipment until serviced by an electrician; maintain unobstructed access to all electrical panels; refer wiring or electrical modifications to the Electronics Shop or Building Coordinator; and avoid extension cords, which should not go under doors, across aisles, hang from the ceiling, or plug into other extension cords.

provisions.section: 3.2.9 Safety Precautions in Chemistry Lab and PCB lab
provisions.text: Chemistry and PCB lab precautions: treat every chemical as hazardous; ensure all chemicals are clearly and currently labeled with substance name, concentration, date and responsible individual; comply with fire regulations on storage quantities, approved containers and cabinets and labeling; use volatile and flammable compounds only in a fume hood and perform aerosol-producing procedures in a hood; never allow a solvent to contact skin and always use gloves; never smell a solvent - read the label; dispose of waste and broken glassware in proper containers; clean up spills immediately; and do not store food in laboratories.

policies.name: Disciplinary Policy - Rules of Discipline for Students
policies.purpose: Rules of discipline students must observe and the actions taken for violation.
policies.scope: All students; parents and guardians are requested to direct their wards to observe these rules.
aliases: what happens if i break the rules

provisions.text: Students must attend lectures, practicals, tutorials etc. as per the Time Table.

Students whose attendance and/or progress in various tests and examinations is not satisfactory, and who do not perform the required number of tutorials and/or practicals, are likely to lose their terms. Students who do not submit term work in required subjects are likely to lose their term. Prolonged absence, even on grounds of ill health, may also lead to loss of terms.
Defaulter students will be detained and will not be allowed to appear for the university examinations.
Students should not get involved in ragging activities. If found, strict action will be taken.
Every student must wear a clean and decent dress while coming to the College. Three-fourth pants and sleeveless dresses are not allowed.

Every student must wear the Identity Card as long as he or she is in the College campus, and must produce it whenever demanded by a member of the teaching or non-teaching staff. In case of loss of Identity Card the matter should be immediately reported to the Principal and an application made for a new Identity Card, which will be issued on payment of charges.
provisions.ambiguity: The replacement charge amount is NOT SPECIFIED IN SOURCE.

provisions.text: No student may display any notice, circular, poster or banner in the College premises without the prior permission of the Principal. Outsiders are not permitted in the College premises without the prior permission of the Principal. All meetings, cultural programs, debates and elocutions organized on College premises must be held in the presence of teaching staff members and with the prior permission of the Principal.
Students must take proper care of College property. Strict action will be taken against students damaging College property and they will be required to compensate for the damage.

Smoking is strictly prohibited in the College premises. Use of mobile telephones is strictly prohibited in classrooms, laboratories and the library. Students must not loiter on the floors while classes are going on.

The following actions may be taken if a student violates the rules of discipline: (1) warning to the student; (2) warning to the student as well as a letter to the parents; (3) cancellation of terms; (4) refusal of admission in the next term or academic year; (5) cancellation of admission.

policies.name: Anti-Plagiarism Policy
policies.purpose: Definition of plagiarism, the enquiry mechanism and the actions that may be initiated.
policies.scope: Academic work including paper presentation, thesis, dissertations, projects, articles and experimental data. The stated enquiry and penalties are framed for a faculty member.

provisions.text: Plagiarism is using the work of another person, without their permission or information, and presenting it as your own. It is most used in the academic world involving paper presentation, thesis, dissertations, projects, articles and experimental data.

The Principal may constitute a 'Plagiarism Enquiry Committee' which is a permanent standing committee to which all complaints may be submitted. The Committee may also have the Head of the concerned Department as a Special Invitee. This committee conducts the enquiry of alleged plagiarism and submits its report to the Principal within a week, recommending appropriate disciplinary action depending on the gravity of the case.

numbers.of: deadline for the committee to submit its enquiry report

provisions.text: On receipt of a written complaint from the aggrieved person, the Principal instructs the committee in writing to conduct an enquiry and recommend appropriate disciplinary action within 4 weeks. The Committee may call for written statements from the persons involved and adduce evidence; notice has to be issued to both parties to record their versions and statements. Based on the enquiry the Committee may recommend suitable action for approval by the Principal. The Principal, with the consent of the Governing Body, may order enforcement of the actions suggested.

numbers.of: deadline to complete enquiry and recommend action

provisions.text: During the enquiry period the alleged faculty member is asked to proceed on leave without pay until the enquiry committee submits its report to the Principal and recommends appropriate action.

If plagiarism is established, the following actions can be initiated against the person involved depending on the Plagiarism Enquiry Committee's recommendation: (1) demotion, warning, fine, penalty or a combination; (2) termination or cessation of services; (3) in case of termination, the faculty shall not be given a recommendation letter by the Principal for future employment in India or abroad; (4) the Principal may report the incident to the appropriate law enforcing authority.
The Library has procured Urkund anti-plagiarism software for checking plagiarism in research papers and project documents.

policies.purpose: Meet the needs of upgrading and creating infrastructure that supports quality education and a good teaching-learning environment.
policies.scope: Obligatory for K. J. Somaiya Institute of Engineering and Information Technology; framed by the management.

provisions.text: As per the Infrastructure Policy, the foresight planning of the Ayurvihar campus should be displayed at the entrance and at various places in the Institute. The infrastructure policy framed by the management is obligatory for KJSIEIT.

The Estate Committee is constituted to discuss and take decisions regarding infrastructure development and renovation. It involves the head of the institute, two senior professors from the institute, members of the trust project office (chief engineer, civil engineer and architect) and a management representative. Committee members meet as per need to review and place proposals regarding infrastructure requirements.

provisions.text: Objectives: meet the needs of upgrading/creating infrastructure that supports quality education and promotes a good teaching-learning environment; allocate funds for infrastructure development; and look after optimum utilization of resources to carry out curricular, co-curricular, extra-curricular and research activities.

Infrastructure work steps: (1) Work proposal - after complete discussion of requirement, a work proposal with financial details is sent for approval to head office; (2) Budget proposal - the Institute allocates funds for the required work; (3) Quotation - minimum three genuine quotations with full description of work are received in sealed envelopes at the head of the Institute office; (4) Negotiations - unbiased negotiations are conducted in presence of the estate committee; (5) Party selection - a genuine party for the work is selected; (6) Work order - the final work order with signatures of negotiating members is sent for confirmation and signature of the Secretary/Provost of SVV; (7) Contract document - the agreement is made with all terms and conditions and the final work order issued to the selected party; (8) Follow-up with the party to get the work done as per the order issued, with coordination, maintenance and consistent quality check.

policies.purpose: To conduct all examinations with clock precision in a fair and smooth manner and to publish flawless results in stipulated time.
policies.scope: Undergraduate and Post-Graduate Programs, w.e.f. A.Y. 2021-2022, at K J Somaiya Institute of Engineering and Information Technology - an Autonomous Institute affiliated to University of Mumbai.

provisions.text: Objectives of the Examination Manual: (a) to conduct all the examinations with clock precision in a fair and smooth manner; (b) to publish flawless results in stipulated time.

Assessment of student learning should be a fair and transparent process which follows University, College and Government regulations so that students are treated impartially across the institution. This document incorporates all of the policies, rules and procedures relating to processes of examination and evaluation which are approved by the Academic Council.

K.J. Somaiya Institute of Engineering and Information Technology shall implement the Choice Based Credit & Grading System (CBCGS) Scheme I 2021-2022 for Undergraduate and Post-graduate Programmes in Engineering and Technology, being an autonomous institute.

A course credit is a unit that gives weightage to the value, level or time requirements of an academic course measured for obtaining a particular degree. A student must complete the assigned academic activities for all prescribed courses to earn the required number of credits. The number of credits assigned for a course is based on the number of contact hours per week for that course; the credit structure and its allotment is specified in the syllabus scheme of each semester.

Continuous Assessment includes TEST 1 (T1) and TEST 2 (T2): two tests in a semester. For core courses each test is conducted for 15 marks; for basic fundamental courses each test is conducted for 10 marks.
provisions.superseded_note: Superseded for Scheme III (2023-24 onwards) where core tests are 20 marks and fundamental tests 15 marks.

provisions.text: Internal Assessment includes MCQ Tests, Assignments, Quizzes, Presentations, Seminars etc. as prescribed in the syllabus, and shall be of a total of 10 marks for all Theory Courses.
SAT (Skill-based, Activity-based, Technology-based) courses will have an Internal Assessment / Term Work of a total of 20 marks each, as mentioned in the syllabus and examination scheme.
provisions.superseded_note: Superseded for Scheme III where SAT courses carry Term Work of 25 marks.

provisions.text: PBL (Project Based Learning) courses - PBL mini, minor and major - will have an Internal Assessment of 10 marks each.

provisions.text: The weightage shall be: Continuous Assessment (CA) 40% and End Semester Examination (ESE) 60%.
