provisions.text: Progression (ATKT) for UG: a learner who has passed semesters I and II may enter semester III; a learner who has failed in NOT MORE THAN SIX heads of passing, of which NOT MORE THAN THREE are End Semester Examination heads of Semesters I and II considered together, is also permitted to enter semester III. The same six-heads/three-ESE-heads rule applies for entering semester V (on Semesters III and IV, provided semesters I and II are passed) and semester VII (on Semesters V and VI, provided all examinations up to and including semester IV are passed).

numbers.of: maximum total failed heads for progression
maximum failed End Semester Examination heads

provisions.superseded_note: Under the earlier University of Mumbai ordinances (O.6242-O.6244) the limits were EIGHT heads of which not more than FIVE in End Semester Examinations.

provisions.text: Eligibility Criteria Chart (heads failed in Test/Oral/Practical, heads failed in End Semester Exam, total heads, outcome): 3 + 3 = 6 Eligible; 4 + 2 = 6 Eligible; 5 + 1 = 6 Eligible; 6 + 0 = 6 Eligible; 2 + 4 = 6 NOT Eligible; 1 + 5 = 6 NOT Eligible; 0 + 6 = 6 NOT Eligible. Six total heads is always the limit, but more than three failed End Semester Examination heads makes a student ineligible regardless of the total.

Continuous Assessment, End Semester Examination, Practical and/or Oral, and Practical & Oral are considered separate Heads of passing prescribed in the scheme of examinations. Term Work is NOT a separate head of passing; however a learner is eligible to appear for any form of examination only after satisfactory completion of Term Work in all courses of that semester.

A learner must obtain a minimum of 45% of the full marks assigned to pass in individual courses of semester I to III examinations, and must obtain a minimum of 45% separately in Continuous Assessment, End Semester Examination, Practical and/or Oral examination, Seminar, PBL-Dissertation I & II and Viva voce in each course as applicable. A learner who fails to obtain 45% for seminar, dissertation or viva voce shall improve and resubmit the dissertation or submit another dissertation in subsequent semesters.

numbers.of: minimum marks to pass each PG head

provisions.text: Credit for a course is obtained using a multiplier of one for lecture and tutorial hours and half for laboratory hours. Seminars typically carry 3 credits. PBL-Dissertation I carries 12 credits and Dissertation-II carries 15 credits. The minimum credit required for award of the Master of Technology programme is 68.

A Supplementary Examination is conducted in July/August (for backlog of even semesters) and in December/January (for backlog of odd semesters) for all courses of all M.Tech Semester I and II programs for learners who failed or remained absent in the regular exam. Backlog examinations for such candidates will NOT be conducted in November/December or May/June. The Supplementary Examination counts as a second attempt. The regular exam grade table and grace mark rules (only ordinance O.5042-A Resolution by Evaluators) apply.
provisions.ambiguity: This supplementary-examination rule is stated for M.Tech Semester I & II only. No equivalent supplementary-examination rule for B.Tech is stated in this document or in the handbook.

provisions.text: A learner who has passed the M.Tech degree examination and wishes to improve CGPI may appear again for the existing examination with the available courses. Grade improvement and performance improvement are available only in Semester II of M.Tech for a learner who has appeared for the regular examination. In Grade Improvement, previous marks for that course are overwritten by the new marks and other marks are carried forward with a + sign; the Result Gazette is titled 'Grade Improvement'. In Performance Improvement, with all theory courses and all OR/PR examinations, the performance is treated as a fresh/first attempt with no carried-forward indication, and Term Work and Continuous Assessment (T1 & T2, SAT & PBL) marks are carried forward; the Result Gazette is titled 'Performance Improvement'.

Grace marks for passing in each course/head of passing (Theory/Practical/Oral/Test) in the End Semester Examination: up to 50 marks head = 2 grace marks; 51-100 = 3; 101-150 = 4; 151-200 = 5; 201-250 = 6; 251-300 = 7; 301-350 = 8; 351-400 = 9; 401 and above = 10. These grace marks may be awarded by Resolution by the evaluators subject to passing of the course, based on the examiner's written consent. The benefit across different heads shall not exceed 1% of the aggregate marks in that examination, and applies only if the candidate passes the entire examination of the semester/year. The result gazette is marked with @ if the candidate passes with grace marks under this ordinance.

numbers.of: maximum grace marks for a head above 400 marks

provisions.text: If a candidate fails in only ONE course/head of passing having passed all others, the deficiency of marks in that head may be condoned by not more than 1% of the aggregate marks of the examination or 10% of the total marks of that head, whichever is less. Condonation is restricted to a maximum of 10 marks only. Condonation is shown in the result gazette and grade card with an asterisk and the ordinance number (O.5045).

numbers.of: maximum failed heads eligible for condonation
maximum condonation as share of that head's marks

provisions.text: Ordinance O.229 Sports Grace: candidates are eligible for up to a maximum of 10 grace marks for participation in any ONE of: (a) reaching quarter-final at intercollegiate sports or one of the eight places in an individual sport event, or representing the University at inter-state, zonal, national or international level, certified by the Director of Physical Education & Sports; (b) securing first three positions in cultural group events or first three places in an individual cultural event, or adjudged best Actor/Actress, Music Director, Lighting/Sound operator, Author, Choreographer or Director, or representing the University in cultural events, certified by the Head of the concerned Section; (c) being a member of students' councils under Section 40 of the Maharashtra Universities Act 1994 and actively participating. Under CBGS, instead of 10 grace marks in the total, an additional 0.1 point is added to the SGPI if the candidate has cleared all heads of passing. In case of failure in one or more heads, the benefit is granted to the extent of 5% of the maximum marks allotted to that head. The benefit is available only on a first attempt at an End Semester Examination. Grace marks under this ordinance are shown separately with the sign # and are not counted for scholarships, prizes, medals or other awards. Combined benefit of sports grace and semester grace can be given only if the candidate has passed in all heads except TWO before applying sports grace.

numbers.of: CBGS equivalent of the 10 grace marks
grace as share of head marks when failing a head

provisions.section: 3. Instructions for Students while Appearing for End Semester Examination
provisions.text: Examination hall rules: candidates must be present at the centre at least 30 minutes before the start and are given entry to the block 15 minutes before the examination commences; they must carry the student ID card and hall ticket; they must not carry any electronic gadget such as mobile phone, smart watch or tablet, or any reading material - possession is treated as malpractice; bags and belongings are deposited in the designated area at the candidate's own risk; candidates occupy the seat per the displayed seating plan and sign against their seat number on the attendance sheet; on the first page of the answer book only the program, semester details, course and number of supplementary sheets may be written - any extra writing anywhere in the answer book is treated as unfair means; candidates hold no communication with anyone other than the Block Supervisor; nothing may be written on the question paper or hall ticket; candidates may leave only after 30 minutes from the start and only on submitting the answer book, and may not leave in the last ten minutes; and the supervisor may deny entrance to a candidate arriving later than 30 minutes after the start.

numbers.of: reporting time before exam and minimum time before leaving
period at the end when leaving is not allowed

provisions.text: Leaving the examination hall to visit the washroom is not allowed in the first one and a half hours of the examination and in the last 15 minutes towards the end of the examination.

numbers.of: initial period when washroom visits are not allowed
final period when washroom visits are not allowed

provisions.text: Dos: enter the exam hall 15 minutes before the examination; carry ID card and hall ticket; use the washroom before or after the exam; bring plain water in a transparent bottle and no food items or beverages; leave bags in the designated area; comply with invigilators' instructions; maintain decorum; co-operate during frisking. Don'ts: do not carry bags, purses, mobile phones, any kind of watches, calculator cover, paper or opaque plastic covers/pouches or paper of any kind inside the hall; do not wear an apron, jacket, hoody or other clothing accessories; do not write anything on your hand or body or on the question paper; do not talk during examinations; do not resort to malpractice/unfair means; do not resort to misconduct or misbehaviour. Indulging in any kind of malpractice or unfair means will lead to the result being declared 'null & void' as per rule.

provisions.section: 5. General Instructions to Students for Open House
provisions.text: Open House: students must attend in person as per the time table displayed on the department notice board; no one except the student - not parents, guardians, friends or representatives - may attend; students sign an attendance sheet at the venue; once inside the classroom students may not leave unless they return the answer books, and the answer book may not be taken outside; no food or drinking water is allowed; students may not carry a pen, pencil or any writing material to avoid tampering - doing so is treated as Unfair Means; no electronic gadgets such as camera, mobile phone or smart watch are allowed and photographing any part of the answer book is treated as Unfair Means; the college is not responsible for belongings.

Student grievances are NOT resolved at the Open House. Students must fill a Grievance Form provided by the teacher in the room. Grievances that can be reported in the ESE Grievance Form are: a difference between the ESE marks on the answer book and those displayed on the intranet; Re-verification (totalling mistake, unassessed part); and Re-assessment (grievances related to the marking scheme). A student who has filled the grievance form in Category III may not also fill it in Category II. Forms are submitted to the faculty/staff present in the classroom; pens are provided by the college.

The student makes the necessary payment of rechecking fees for getting the answer paper rechecked, and the result is revised only if the student has passed in the process of rechecking. If any discrepancy is found in the declared UG/PG results, the results are amended after due verification.
provisions.ambiguity: The rechecking fee amount is NOT SPECIFIED IN SOURCE in this document. The 2018 handbook states Rs. 500 per subject for revaluation and Rs. 100 per application for a photocopy, under the then-applicable University of Mumbai procedure.

provisions.text: All Grievance forms are thoroughly examined by the Controller of Examinations (COE) and/or by the Examination and Evaluation Committee (EEC). The decision of the committee will be an increase, decrease or no change in the marks after reassessment, and Unfair Means reported if any.

Unfair means includes: possessing unfair means material (books, written chits, electronic gadgets such as mobile phone or smart watch) and/or copying from it; transcribing unauthorized material; intimidating, using obscene language, threatening or using violence against an invigilator, manhandling them, leaving the hall without permission or causing disturbance; unauthorized communication with other examinees or anyone inside or outside the hall; mutual or mass copying; smuggling answer books out or in as copying material; smuggling in a blank or written answer book and forging the Junior Supervisor's signature; interfering with or counterfeiting the college seal, answer books or office stationery; inserting currency notes in answer books or attempting to bribe; impersonation; revealing identity in any form in the answer book; and any other similar act considered unfair means by the competent authority.

On unfair means the Chief Conductor: calls on the student to surrender the unfair means material and the answer book; obtains the student's signature on the materials and list, countersigned by the Senior Supervisor and Chief Conductor; records the student's statement and undertaking and the statements of the Junior and Senior Supervisors in writing; and takes one or more decisions depending on gravity - in case of impersonation or violence, expel the student from the examination and bar them from the remaining examination; obtain an undertaking that the competent authority's decision is final and allow the student to continue; report the case to the police under Maharashtra Act No. XXXI of 1982; or confiscate the answer book, mark it 'suspected unfair means case' and issue a fresh answer book. All materials, the undertaking and the answer book are forwarded in a separate confidential sealed envelope marked 'Suspected unfair means case'.

The Principal, as competent authority for college examinations, after considering the Committee's report may grant benefit of doubt, issue a warning, exonerate, or impose one or more of: annulment of the student's performance in full or in part; debarring the student from appearing for any examination of the College for a stipulated period not exceeding five years; debarring the student from taking admission for any course for a stipulated period not exceeding five years; cancellation of College scholarships, awards, prizes or medals awarded in that examination; and a fine, with additional punishment if the fine is not paid within the stipulated period.

Quantum of punishment (Appendix A): possession of copying material - annulment of performance at the College Examination in full (this also applies in addition to items 2-14); possession plus actual copying - exclusion from the College Examinations concerned for ONE subsequent examination; possession of another student's answer book or supplementary sheet - exclusion of BOTH students for ONE subsequent examination; the same with evidence of copying - exclusion of both for TWO subsequent examinations; mutual/mass copying - exclusion of all students for TWO subsequent examinations; smuggling answer books in or out - TWO subsequent examinations; smuggling in a written answer book based on the question paper set - THREE subsequent examinations; smuggling in a written answer book and forging the Junior Supervisor's signature - FOUR; attempting to forge the Junior Supervisor's signature - FOUR; counterfeiting the college seal, answer books or stationery - FOUR; answer book or supplementary sheet taken outside the hall or any other insertion - FOUR; inserting currency notes or bribing - FOUR (the money is credited to the Students Welfare Fund); obscene language or violent threats inside the hall - FOUR; impersonation - FIVE subsequent examinations (both students if the impersonator is a college learner); revealing the candidate's identity in the answer book - annulment in full; anything written on the body or clothes - annulment in full; making an appeal to the examiner by any mode of communication - annulment in full; any other malpractice - annulment in full and severe punishment depending on gravity.

'Annulment of Performance in full' includes the student's performance at the theory examination but does NOT include performance at term work, project work with its term work, oral or practical, and dissertation examinations, unless malpractice was used there. A student involved in malpractice at Practical/Dissertation/Project examinations is dealt with as per the punishment provided for the theory examination.

If disciplinary action was previously taken against a student for malpractice during an examination and the student is caught again, they shall be dealt with severely. Enhanced punishment may extend to double the punishment provided for the offence committed at the second or subsequent examination.

numbers.of: maximum multiplier of the prescribed punishment for a repeat offence

policies.name: Examination Policies (2018 edition, University of Mumbai affiliated scheme)
policies.purpose: Examination conduction, assessment, grading and eligibility rules as published in the 2018 Second Publication of the handbook.
policies.scope: Four year semester-wise degree course academically affiliated to Mumbai University. First Year and Fourth Year examinations conducted by the University under CAP; Second and Third Year conducted in college under CAS.
policies.version_note: SUPERSEDED. This chapter describes KJSIEIT as academically affiliated to Mumbai University with IA 20% / ESE 80% and an eight-head ATKT rule. KJSIT is now autonomous with CA 40% / ESE 60% and a six-head ATKT rule. Retained for version history; do NOT answer a current student's question from it.

provisions.text: A four year, semester-wise degree course is run at KJSIEIT, Sion, academically affiliated to Mumbai University. First Year (semesters I and II) and Fourth Year (semesters VII and VIII) examinations are conducted by the University, which sets and assesses the papers under CAP and awards the statement of marks and degree. Second Year (semesters III and IV) and Third Year (semesters V and VI) examinations are conducted in college; papers are set by the University and assessed in college under CAS, and statements of marks are awarded by the college on behalf of the University.
Odd semester examinations are held in the second half of the year, in November/December, and even semester examinations in the first half of the year, in May/June of every year.

The Principal is the Chief Conductor of Examinations. Faculties are appointed as Senior Supervisor and Junior Supervisor while lab assistants are appointed as Understudy Supervisors. The University appoints a Joint Chief Conductor from another institute to observe proceedings. In every block one Junior Supervisor is present, and each block has a capacity of a maximum of 40 students.

numbers.of: maximum capacity of an examination block

provisions.text: Students are not allowed to leave the examination room until 30 minutes after the start of the examination. The supervisor can also deny entrance to a student who arrives later than 30 minutes after the start of the examination.

numbers.of: minimum time before leaving and maximum lateness allowed

provisions.text: Students are required to have suitable identification - the student I.D. card and Hall Ticket - available during examinations. The Block Supervisor may request students to produce identification. If a student claims not to have proof of identity, they may be required to present suitable I.D. at a mutually agreeable time and place, and failure to appear constitutes an irregularity reported to the Chief Conductor.

After the examination, answer books are tallied with the attendance sheet. Answer books for Second and Third year papers are masked and coded to hide the student's identity for fair evaluation, while First and Fourth year papers are sent to the University on the same day. All marked final examination papers, together with the tally sheets and final examination questions, are retained in the Examination Cell for a period of at least one year following the examination period.
Under the 2018 scheme, Internal Assessment carried 20% weightage and the End Semester Examination 80%.
provisions.superseded_note: SUPERSEDED by CA 40% / ESE 60% under the autonomous CBCGS schemes.

provisions.text: Attendance for all - theory, tutorial, practical and examination - is compulsory as per University Ordinance 119; 75% is compulsory for keeping term.

numbers.of: University of Mumbai ordinance governing attendance

provisions.text: 2018 letter grade and grade point allocation: 80.00 and above = O, 10, Outstanding; 75.00-79.99 = A, 9, Excellent; 70.00-74.99 = B, 8, Very Good; 60.00-69.99 = C, 7, Good; 50.00-59.99 = D, 6, Fair; 45.00-49.99 = E, 5, Average; 40.00-44.99 = P, 4, Pass; less than 40 = F, 0, Fail. AB is Absent with 0 grade point and the student should reappear for that exam in due course.
provisions.superseded_note: SUPERSEDED - see the B.Tech grade table w.e.f. 2024-25.

provisions.text: Internal Assessment and End Semester Examination are two separate heads for passing. Practical and/or oral exams are also independent heads of passing. A learner should satisfactorily complete Term Work in all courses for a particular semester as per the syllabus to be eligible to appear for any form of examination.

provisions.section: 6.4.9 Promotion of Learner and Award of Grades
provisions.text: A learner is declared PASS and eligible for a grade in a particular course if they secure at least 40% marks in each head of passing, OR secure more than 50% in total (IA + ESE) if the learner fails in IA. Internal Assessment or End Semester Examination marks are carried over in the next exam if one head shows PASS.

numbers.of: minimum marks in each head of passing
alternative total (IA+ESE) threshold when failing IA

provisions.text: Re-examination for Internal Assessment should be completed before the commencement of the next semester theory examination. Re-examination for the End Semester Examination is conducted as per the schedule planned by the University of Mumbai.

Under the 2018 rule a student qualifies for ATKT if they fail in not more than 8 heads of passing, of which not more than 5 heads are inclusive of End Semester Examination together, for the academic year (2 semesters). 'AB' is considered for the lecture in deciding ATKT.

numbers.of: maximum failed ESE heads for ATKT (2018)

provisions.superseded_note: SUPERSEDED by the current six-heads / three-ESE-heads rule under KJSIT autonomy.

provisions.text: At the end of each semester a grade report reflecting the learner's performance in that semester is prepared and issued. It includes fail grades as awarded. Even when a failed course is passed in a later semester, no new modified grade report is issued for the earlier semester; for backlog courses a separate grade report card is issued when the course is passed. The grade card shows the Letter Grade, Credit points at individual courses, SGPI for each semester and CGPI for all successfully completed courses till that semester's examination.

The Examination Cell is headed by the In charge Examination (I.E.) from faculty with 5 supporting staff (3 clerks, 1 peon and 1 faculty as assistant). Its functions include receiving circulars, guidelines, office orders and notifications; forwarding examination notices to departments; displaying notices on exam form submission, fee collection, last date of fee collection and modalities of payment of fine; displaying the University time table, invigilation duty chart and seat allotment; mobilizing staff and assigning examination duties; conducting the central assessment process; distributing mark sheets to students; result analysis; verification and conduction of the photocopy/revaluation process; and submitting the examination report to the Principal.

policies.name: Photocopy and Revaluation of Answer Books
policies.purpose: Rules and procedure for providing photocopies of assessed answer books and for revaluation, bringing transparency to the examination system.
policies.scope: Theory papers and scripts of practical examination, sessional work, project work, dissertation, internal assessment and term work of all examinations conducted by the college on behalf of the University, in the current session. Under University of Mumbai circular VCD/1 of 2016.
policies.version_note: AMBIGUOUS / REQUIRES VERIFICATION for current students. This is the University of Mumbai VCD/1 of 2016 procedure as published in the 2018 handbook and republished standalone as 'Examination Structure / Code of Conduct'. Under KJSIT autonomy the current published process is the Open House plus ESE Grievance Form handled by the COE/EEC, and the current document does not state a revaluation fee. Whether these Rs. 500 / Rs. 100 fees and 10-working-day windows still apply is not established by any current source.

provisions.text: Applying for a photocopy of the answer book and applying for revaluation are two independent processes. Having a photocopy is not a pre-requisite for applying for revaluation. The examinee can independently apply for revaluation, or a photocopy, or both simultaneously. An examinee who applies for revaluation must note that their original marks become null and void as soon as the application for revaluation is submitted.

Within ten working days from the date of declaration of the results or the issue of the statement of marks by the college, the candidate may apply in the prescribed format with a non-refundable fee of Rs. 100 by cash or DD drawn in favour of the 'Principal, KJSIEIT' payable at Mumbai. Examinees belonging to reserved categories are granted a 50% concession in fee. For University examinations the college forwards Rs. 80 per photocopy to the Controller of Examinations and retains Rs. 20 per photocopy as administrative expenses.

numbers.of: fee concession for reserved category examinees
deadline to apply for a photocopy

provisions.text: The College shall endeavour to supply photocopies of answer books as far as possible within twenty five working days from the date of receipt of the application. The Principal publishes the list of students whose photocopies are ready for delivery on the notice board. The photocopy is handed over to the applicant examinee in person only and under no circumstances to any other person, on producing the original receipt of the application and establishing identity.

numbers.of: target time to supply a photocopy

provisions.ambiguity: The source text reads 'within twenty (25) working days' - the word and the numeral disagree; the numeral 25 is used consistently elsewhere in the same clause.

provisions.text: On receipt of the photocopy the applicant examinee is the sole custodian of it, shall not part with custody or possession of it, and shall not use it for any other purpose. Neither the examinee nor any other person can use the copy to dispute or challenge the quality of assessment or quantum of marks assigned.

If the examinee is found guilty of indulging in any unfair act or attempt, they are tried before the Unfair Means Inquiry Committee of the college and the authorities' decision is final. If proved, the examinee is liable for punishment ranging from cancellation of marks in that subject (whether originally granted or granted on revaluation), annulment of examinations for a stipulated period of up to 5 examinations, or cancellation of the result of the examination.

If on receipt of the photocopy the examinee notices a mistake in totalling, non-assessment of a question or sub-question, or an improper photocopy, they should apply to the Principal, KJSIEIT in the prescribed form with the photocopy and a copy of the question paper within seven working days from the date of publication of the notice by the Principal. After due verification the Principal makes the necessary rectification in the marks and consequently in the result, without charging any further fee.

numbers.of: deadline to report a discrepancy in the photocopy

provisions.text: In case of non-assessment of a question or sub-question the original assessor, or the moderator if the answer book was moderated, is called for rectification. It is binding on the examiner or moderator to attend and on the Principal of another college to relieve them, on the given date or within three working days if no specific date is communicated. The examiner is entitled to travelling allowance only. Not attending within the stipulated period is treated as misconduct and a penalty of Rs. 100 per day is imposed on all concerned, recovered from pay and remitted to the college where the examiner was called, to be credited to the Students' Welfare Account or the Library Account.

numbers.of: penalty for an examiner not attending a recall
default time to attend a recall

provisions.text: An examinee not satisfied with the marks awarded may independently apply for revaluation to the college in the prescribed form, whether or not they applied for a photocopy. All examinees may apply for revaluation with whatever marks they secured, even zero marks, and for as many subjects as they desire. The prescribed form is obtained from the office of the college. The duly filled and signed form is submitted to the college office with the statement of marks, prescribed fees and the question papers for which revaluation is sought, within ten working days from the date of declaration of the result or the date the college issued the statement of marks, whichever is later. Incomplete forms or forms without relevant documents may be rejected without assigning any reason.

The non-refundable prescribed fee for revaluation is Rs. 500 per subject per answer book, paid in cash or by DD drawn in favour of the Principal of the college. Examinees from reserved categories are given a fifty per cent concession provided a certified copy of the caste certificate is enclosed. For University examinations the college forwards Rs. 450 per subject to the Controller of Examinations and retains Rs. 50 per subject as administrative expenses.

numbers.of: revaluation fee per subject per answer book
fee concession for reserved category examinees

provisions.text: The marks obtained after revaluation are accepted by the Principal if the marks assigned as a result of revaluation increase or decrease by ten per cent or more than the marks originally obtained in the paper without any grace; in such cases the original marks are treated as null and void. Fractions are ignored when computing the ten per cent difference. The revaluation marks are also accepted if the candidate gets the benefit of passing the subject or examination, or a change of class or grade, with or without grace marks.

numbers.of: minimum change for revaluation marks to be accepted

provisions.text: A difference between the original marks and the revaluation marks is accepted up to twenty five per cent of the maximum marks assigned to that paper. If the difference increases or decreases by twenty five per cent of the maximum marks, a second revaluation is done by a third examiner from the panel, and the AVERAGE of the first and second revaluations is accepted as the final marks. An answer book is also sent for second revaluation to another senior examiner if on the first revaluation the candidate's marks are decreased below the passing marks or below the marks required for securing a class; in that case the third examiner's marks are treated as final.

numbers.of: change in maximum paper marks that triggers a second revaluation

provisions.topic: no photocopy of revalued answer book
provisions.text: Answer books already revaluated shall not be moderated or further re-revaluated, unless so directed by the Vice-Chancellor in exceptional cases. THE PHOTOCOPY OR COPIES OF THE REVALUATED ANSWER BOOKS SHALL NOT BE PROVIDED TO THE EXAMINEES.
The whole process of revaluation shall be completed as far as possible within a period of forty five days from the date of receipt of the application for revaluation by the college.

Pending the process of revaluation, and subject to availability of seats, a student may be admitted to the next higher class to which they could have been admitted had they passed or been granted ATKT, if they had originally obtained the required passing marks in the papers for which revaluation was applied. The college may charge a fee of Rs. 500 at the time of granting such admission. The admission is provisional and stands automatically cancelled on receipt of the revaluation result if the student is not declared passed in the requisite number of subjects; in that case the fees collected are not refunded. Such students may appear at the next class examination, but their results are declared only on passing the requisite number of subjects on revaluation; otherwise their admission and results are treated as null and void. If the student is declared passed, the provisional admission is regularized and the amount is adjusted against the fees the college is entitled to collect, with any balance refunded for reserved category or fee-concession students.

The remuneration for appointed examiners is Rs. 20 per answer book and Rs. 120 as travelling allowance per day, or a lump sum of Rs. 320 if the number of answer books is less than 10. Examiners from the same college are not entitled to the travelling allowance.

numbers.of: lump sum for fewer than 10 answer books

policies.name: Examination Ordinances - Grace Marks, Condonation and Moderation (2018)
policies.purpose: University of Mumbai ordinances on grace marks, condonation, moderation and malpractice as adopted in the 2018 handbook.

provisions.text: Ordinance O.5043A - Grace Marks for getting Higher Class/Grade: a candidate who passes all subjects and heads of passing without the benefit of gracing or condonation, and whose total marks fall short of securing Second Class, Higher Second Class, First Class or the next higher grade by not more than 1% of the aggregate marks of that examination or up to 10 marks, whichever is less, shall be given the required marks to get the next higher class or grade. The benefit is not given if the candidate fails to secure the necessary passing marks in the aggregate course or head of passing.

numbers.of: maximum grace as share of aggregate marks
absolute maximum grace for a higher class

provisions.text: Ordinance O.5044A - Grace Marks for getting distinction / Grade 'O' in the subject or course only: a candidate who passes all courses or heads of passing without the benefit of gracing or condonation, and whose total marks in a course fall short by not more than three marks for getting Grade 'O' or distinction, shall be given the necessary grace marks up to three in a maximum of two subjects or courses, subject to a maximum of 1% of the total marks of that head of passing, whichever is more.

numbers.of: maximum grace per subject for distinction
maximum subjects that may receive distinction grace

provisions.text: Ordinance O.5045A - Condonation: if a candidate fails in only one course or head of passing having passed all others, the deficiency of marks in that head may be condoned by not more than 1% of the aggregate marks of the examination or 10% of the total marks of that head, whichever is less. Condonation is restricted to a maximum of 10 marks only and is shown in the grade card or statement of marks as an asterisk with the ordinance number.

Ordinance O.5046A - Moderation: the moderation system is applicable to all faculties for Undergraduate and Post Graduate Semester End Examinations and External Theory Examinations. 100% moderation of the answer book is carried out for candidates failing by 10% of the aggregate marks of that course or paper.

provisions.text: For investigating unfair means at an examination held by the College, the Unfair Means Inquiry Committee appointed by the College consists of five teachers, other than the Principal, nominated by the Principal, one of whom is designated Chairperson. Members appointed to the College Examination Committee shall not be appointed to the Unfair Means Inquiry Committee. The Committee functions as a recommendatory body and submits its recommendations as a report to the competent authority, which issues final orders on penal action after ensuring reasonable opportunity was given and natural justice followed.

numbers.of: members of the college Unfair Means Inquiry Committee

provisions.text: The Principal or authorized officer informs the student in writing of the alleged act of unfair means and asks them to show cause why the charges should not be held proved and the stipulated punishment imposed. The student may appear before the Inquiry Committee with a written reply, and must present their own case in person. Documents relied upon are shown to the student and evidence is recorded in their presence. Reasonable opportunity including an oral hearing is given. If the student fails to appear after a show cause notice they are given one more opportunity; after two chances the Committee decides in absentia on available evidence, and that decision is binding.

policies.name: Library : Knowledge Resource Hub Policies
policies.purpose: Vision, profile, sections, committee and operating rules of the KJSIEIT Knowledge Resource Hub (Library).
aliases: how many books can i borrow

provisions.text: Vision: KJSIEIT Library desires to set up a Knowledge Resource Centre that will provide free and open access to materials and information that reflect a global perspective. Mission: build effective and efficient digital information resource capacity; establish memberships of other technical libraries for students' benefit; develop an institutional repository including the intellectual assets of the institute; and foster an innovative and collaborative staff culture.

The library holds 22,000 volumes of renowned Indian and foreign authors comprising text books, reference books, handbooks, encyclopedias and general reading books; 6,080 e-books accessible remotely; 500 e-journals including IEEE, ACM, ASME, Springer, Science Direct and IET journals with remote access; the IET Digital Library; NPTEL video lectures by IIT professors; a collection of CDs and DVDs; and 14 subscribed newspapers in Marathi, Hindi, Gujarati and English.

The KJSIEIT Knowledge Resource Centre (Library) is located on the first floor near the auditorium. Its sections are: Acquisition, Processing, Book stack area, Circulation, Journals/Magazine, Reference, Reading room and Digital Library. The library layout also identifies a Lobby, a Staff reading section and a Librarian's room.

The Library Advisory Committee includes the Principal as chairman, one External Advisor, one Internal Advisor, the Librarian as Convenor, one member from each department, a Student Representative and the Assistant Librarian as co-ordinator. It meets at regular intervals to discuss infrastructure, furniture, collection development (books, periodicals and journals), rules, services and policies, and new plans.
Library staff comprises one Librarian, one Assistant Librarian, one Library Assistant, one Library Clerk and two Library Attendants.

KJSIEIT Library follows DDC 22nd edition for classification of books. Books are stamped on three edges, the front page, pages 51, 151, 251, 351 etc. and the last page; titles and details are entered in the Accession register; data entry is done in Bookworm software; card pockets and issue slips are pasted on last pages; call number and date of purchase are written on the title page; spine labels are generated from Bookworm; and all books are bar coded with barcodes pasted on the title page and last page.

Number of books that can be issued at a time and the retention period: Faculty 6 books for 4 months; Faculty pursuing M.E./Ph.D. 9 books for 6 months; Non-Teaching Staff 6 books for 4 months; Students 6 books for 1 month; Book Bank for all students 6 books (one per subject) for one semester; Book Bank for SC/ST students 6 books (one per subject) for one semester. The online facility provides a one-time renewal of the books provided they are not reserved by another user.

maximum books for faculty pursuing M.E./Ph.D.
retention period for faculty pursuing M.E./Ph.D.
retention period for faculty and non-teaching staff

provisions.text: Books are issued on presentation of the library card along with the smart card. Students are instructed to check the books while borrowing and are responsible for any damage or mutilation noticed at the time of return. All staff and students are given RFID Identity cards, and issue of books, periodicals, CDs, syllabi and question papers is done using these cards. Automated circulation is practiced using Bookworm software and CCTV is installed to control the circulation area.
If books are lost, the borrower shall replace the book with the same edition or the latest edition, or pay the cost as per the rules, after getting permission from the Librarian.
Loss of a borrower card should be reported to the librarian in writing. After checking the borrowing register a fresh replacement card is issued on payment of Rs. 50 per card.

numbers.of: replacement fee for a lost library borrower card

provisions.text: Library borrower cards are valid for the respective academic year only and are renewed each year. At the beginning of the academic year borrower cards should be renewed by producing the fee receipt.
Each student shall obtain a No Dues certificate from the library after returning all issued books, surrendering the borrower's cards and paying outstanding dues, if any.

Students should handle books and journals very carefully. Marking with pencil, writing or highlighting, tearing pages or mutilating them in any other way will be viewed very seriously, and the reader is held responsible unless these are brought to the notice of library staff at the time of issue.

The reading room for students accommodates 100 students. Timings: regular college working days 8.00 a.m. to 7.00 p.m.; holidays (during examination only) 10.00 a.m. to 5.00 p.m. A separate section is set aside for teachers.

numbers.of: reading room opening on working days
reading room closing on working days

provisions.text: Rules for the reading section: silence has to be maintained; no discussion is permitted inside the library; every staff member and student must scan their identity card on the RFID machine at the entrance counter before entering; using cellular phones and audio instruments with or without speaker or headphone is strictly prohibited in the library premises; smoking, sleeping, eating and having refreshments are not allowed; take care of the books and journals; use the rack at the entrance for personal belongings; and switch off fans and lights after use.

Ten PCs are allotted for the Digital Library, which students can use for project work, e-book reference and OPAC search. Rules for using the internet in the library: internet chats, messengers and games are prohibited; changing any setting on any machine is prohibited; downloading any software is prohibited, whether from your disk or the web; computers are designated for academic use only; do not install or uninstall any program or service; and a non-working device should not be fixed individually but reported at the reference desk.

The Online Public Access Catalogue (OPAC) is used for searching books and is available on the Somaiya Vidyavihar website at http://opac.somaiya.edu/. The EBSCO Web Discovery Tool is used to search all resources of all the Somaiya Libraries.

Online journals available remotely at https://library.somaiya.edu/user/login: ACM Digital Library, McGraw Hill Access Engineering Library, Science Direct, Springer (Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Mechanical), ASME, DELNET, IEEE Electronic Library, Wiley E Journals and IET Journals. Remote access is via the Somaiya mail id.

policies.purpose: Value added services offered to students and staff, book purchase and weeding procedures, and library feedback.

provisions.text: Previous five years' question papers are available in the library, filed semester-wise and further subject-wise. All recent question papers are also available in soft format and a print copy is provided on student demand. Question papers are scanned and uploaded on the Somaiya Digital Repository.

provisions.text: All old and revised syllabus copies for all semesters are available in the library for ready reference.
The Somaiya Digital Repository at http://repository.somaiya.edu/ carries video lectures by institute teachers and guest speakers, and notes and question papers.
Orientation of library resources is done for all students and staff, including an introduction to various library policies and the sections in the library.

Through the Book Bank policy books are issued to students for an entire semester. There are three schemes: (a) funded by the Social Welfare Department, Government of Maharashtra - students enrolled under SC scholarship are eligible, and 5 books for one semester are issued; (b) funded by Vidyarthi Kalyan Bhavan, Mumbai Vidyapeeth - all reserved category students are eligible, and 5 books for one semester are issued; (c) funded by KJSIEIT College - all students of KJSIEIT are eligible; applications are collected from interested students and a set of 5 books is issued to each student for one semester against some charges.

It also states 5 books per scheme, while the circulation table in section 7.5.4 states 6 books (one per subject) for Book Bank - REQUIRES VERIFICATION.

provisions.text: Under the alumni membership two books are issued to a student. A refundable deposit of Rs. 1,500 is collected. The applicant must submit a membership form and an attested copy of their degree certificate along with the deposit. A fine of Rs. 5 per day is charged for late return of books. The membership is valid for one academic year and can be renewed every year. If the student does not want to continue, they should withdraw the deposit money within 3 years after expiry of the membership.

No overdue fine rate for regular students, faculty or non-teaching staff is stated anywhere in the manual, although section 5.1.5 of the Administrative Policies confirms that the Librarian is authorized to collect fines from students and staff.

provisions.text: Students are allowed to use the Somaiya Medical College library, which is open 24x7. Additional reading facility is also provided during examinations.

IIT Chennai has published video lectures by eminent IIT professors. These videos have been purchased and stored on the Local Network and are available offline in college through LAN to students, faculty and staff.

Reminder mails are sent to all readers seven days prior to the due date, and reminder mails for overdue books are sent immediately after the due date. Lists of latest books and journals are sent to all patrons, and content pages of all new journals are scanned and sent as part of the Current Awareness system.

provisions.text: Global Common Circulation (GCC) module: every student, faculty member and staff member is eligible to borrow one book at a time for seven days from any library of Somaiya Trust colleges or schools.

numbers.of: books borrowable at a time under GCC

provisions.text: Book Reservation Facility: a member can reserve a book only if the desired book is not available in the library because it is issued to another member. Once the reserved book is returned, the system sends an email notification to the member who reserved it. A FIFO system is followed for reserved book circulation, and an intimation is sent to the member who has already borrowed the book.

Self-Renewal: a member can renew books themselves through OPAC, provided the book is not in demand or reserved, and the renewal is done before the due date. This facility is availed using the SVV NetID integrated for OPAC login.

Earn and Learn scheme: during the annual library stock verification, students are involved in data entry and book rearrangement. A remuneration of Rs. 75 per hour is given. Students are allowed to work for 2 hours a day and not more than 5 days a week.

KJSIEIT Library has subscribed to memberships of the Institution of Electronics and Telecommunication Engineers (IETE), New Delhi - benefits include the IETE newsletter and one technical journal free of cost, subsidized subscription rates for other IETE publications, concessional rates for seminars and conferences, professional development programs, and benefits of IETE's co-operative agreements with professional bodies in other countries - and of the Developing Library Network (DELNET) - benefits include access to union catalogues and other databases, interlibrary loan and document delivery services, retro-conversion, reference services, professional training and technical support.

A list of required books is prepared with reference to the syllabus, and recommendations are invited from faculty members and sanctioned by HODs. These recommendations are sanctioned in the Library committee meeting followed by approval from the Principal. Publisher-wise quotations from three parties are called; the comparative statement is put before the Purchase committee for negotiation. The application for permission to purchase, with the list of books, quotations, budget copy and minutes of the Library committee meeting, is sent to Head Office through the Principal. After approval the purchase order is sent to the vendor, and payment is made after completion of the order.

Weeding out creates space, saves staff and patron time, and keeps the library appealing and current. Criteria include the library's service responses and goals, the needs and demands of users, availability of more suitable material, budget ability to buy more satisfactory items, the item's relation to others on the subject, cooperative agreements with other libraries, possible future usefulness, availability of more current information on the internet, and interlibrary loan availability. Material is selected for weeding for poor content; outdated or obsolete information (especially computers, law, science, space, health and medicine, technology, travel); trivial subject matter; and poor appearance (worn out or ragged items, poorly bound or printed editions, worn rebound editions with torn pages, scratched CDs or DVDs, old newspapers and magazines). Procedure: the material is gathered, a list is prepared and sanctioned in a Library committee meeting where the mode of disposal is discussed; disposal may include donation to a lower cadre library, or scrapping if the physical condition is bad, with quotations taken before scrapping; necessary approval from the Principal is taken and the status of the books in the database is changed from REGULAR to WITHDRAWN.

Feedback is collected from faculty and students on a regular basis for improvement in library services, facilities, resources and other functions, covering how often the library page on the college website is used, use of electronic journals like IEEE, usefulness of the institutional repository for accessing question papers, quality of library staff service, adequacy of reading space and opening hours, how book availability is checked (online catalogue, library staff, browsing the racks), how information about library facilities is obtained (orientation, mails, WhatsApp), National Digital Library of India (NDLI) membership, attendance at the Library Orientation program, and use of the Somaiya Library app available in Google apps.

policies.name: Training and Placement Policies
policies.purpose: To document the systems, procedures and standard operating procedures for assisting students to find placement in industry at the end of the bachelor degree course.
policies.scope: Applicable to all the eligible and interested students and to Placement Committee Members.

provisions.text: Objective: to facilitate placements, and if possible internships, for all interested students by liaising with recruiters and KJSIEIT alumni, with a view towards achieving 100% placements.

The institute intends to help students, whenever possible, to get vacation or concurrent assignments or internships, provided it does not interfere with their regular academic obligations like attendance.
provisions.ambiguity: There is NO internship policy, internship credit rule or internship duration requirement anywhere in this corpus - internships are mentioned only as a best-effort activity subject to attendance.

provisions.text: The Training and Placement Committee (TPCOM) is headed and guided by the Training and Placement Officer. It consists of one faculty member from each department and student volunteers. Faculty representatives for each department are nominated by the Principal in consultation with the concerned Head of Department. Faculty members from each department nominate a minimum of 2 boys and 2 girls from each division as student volunteers who are also part of the placements team. The management and all teaching staff firmly believe that placement is the joint responsibility of all staff members.

The Departmental Placement Coordinator (DPC) is responsible for collection and verification of student data for their department. Work on 'Final year Placements' student data is to be completed BEFORE the students proceed for vacation after the 6th semester examinations.

DPC members maintain resumes of all students eligible for placements in the standardized KJSIEIT format. All students must submit their resumes in the prescribed format as directed by the DPC and furnish proof of details mentioned in the resume for authentication by DPC members. Resumes are updated regularly to include latest results; the resume update window is opened at the discretion of the DPC for interim updates like awards, certifications and live projects. It is the responsibility of the individual student to make and maintain copies of the CV and present it when needed by any company.

After the notice with job profiles and other company details is put up, interested eligible students are asked to sign up. This sign up indicates a commitment on the part of the student to accept an offer by the company in case he or she is selected. Once registered, the student cannot back out midway through a recruitment process.

provisions.topic: backing out of a placement process
provisions.text: Strict action will be taken against defaulters who back out midway through a recruitment process after registering.

Students should be dressed in appropriate formals and assembled for the PPT at least 10 minutes before the scheduled time; late comers will not be entertained once the PPT starts. It is mandatory for all registered students participating in the placement process to attend the PPTs, and only students who attend the PPT are allowed to participate in the placement drive for that company. The Placement Committee takes attendance for each PPT and maintains the record.

numbers.of: how early students must assemble for a PPT

provisions.text: Once a student attends a PPT it is assumed the student has clearly understood all details and accepts the terms and conditions. If something not covered in information shared prior to the PPT is revealed during the PPT and is not acceptable to the student, he or she can back out after informing the placement officer and DPC in writing.

Different companies conduct different selection processes. Usually the process consists of preliminary screening, a written test, a group discussion, a technical interview and an HR interview. The Placement Committee coordinates all these processes and assists students and companies in orderly completion.

Companies taking part on Day ONE give the list of selected students to the placement officer in a sealed envelope; no company can disclose the names of selected students directly. Once processes for all day one companies are over, all offers are displayed simultaneously and the selected students are immediately blocked from other companies' processes. Students securing multiple job offers have to select one and communicate their choice in writing to the placement committee.
One confirmed offer per student is the placement policy, and the student and company are served on a first confirmed offer basis.

If a company is awarded 'DREAM COMPANY' status, the one-offer-per-student rule is relaxed for interested eligible students. Awarding Dream Company status to an organization is at the discretion of the Principal, on recommendation from the placement officer.

For summer assignments and internships, companies are free to disclose the names of selected students on the day they complete their selection process. The selected student is immediately blocked from other companies' processes and is out of the process for further internship opportunities.

Students with a discipline problem at any level may be dropped from further participation in the placement process. Students abandoning a process midway and cases of indiscipline or malpractice will not be eligible for participation in the subsequent placement process.

provisions.topic: no backing out after an offer
provisions.text: If an offer comes to the college from a company through formal or informal communication, it is considered to carry the student's willingness and confirmation to join the company. At this stage, after the offer is received by the institute, the student cannot back out and will be taken out of the Placement Process.
The escalation route for any queries or grievances is: Training and Placement Committee -> Placement officer -> Principal. Grievances are entertained on an individual basis only and not in groups.
Anybody initiating group mails for airing grievances shall be barred from participation in the Placement process.

The Placements notice board, email communications and social media communication from the Placement Committee are the primary mode of communication for all placement related information; all interested students must monitor the notice board and their email ids. All personal queries or additional information required by students should be routed through the Placement Committee alone.
Any student found sharing institute placement information with any external agency or college shall be debarred from participation in the Placement Process.

Email communications to companies are done from the placements id placements.tech@somaiya.edu. Emails are classified as Invitation, Policy/Issue related and routine emails. Invitation and Policy/Issue related mails are handled by the Placement officer only; routine mails may be authorized to be handled by the Training and Placement Committee.

provisions.text: The Student Welfare Policies chapter lists 45 cells, clubs, committees and student professional bodies, numbered 9.1 to 9.45: Student Council; Software Development Cell; Research Development and Consultancy Cell; Training and Placement Cell; Sports Committee; Cultural Committee; ISTE; IEEE; CSI; IET; IETE; IEI; Entrepreneurship Cell; Career Opportunities For Engineers in Public Sector Cell; Cyber Security and Research Cell; Internet of Things Cell; Project Competition Cell; Robotics Cell; Green Club; Technical Committee; Industrial Visit Committee; Intellectual Property Rights Cell; Marathi Bhasha Vangmay Mandal (NAKSHATRA); Magazine Committee; NSS Committee; Robocon Team; Vyom Club; Infinite Loop Club; Team Dramebaaz; New Leap Initiative; College Women Development Cell; Alumni and Corporate Relation Committee; Industry Institute Interaction Cell; Internal Grievance / Complaint Cell; Anti Ragging Committee; Anti Ragging Squad; Institute's Innovation Council (IIC); Career Opportunities for Engineering Students in Public Sector Cell (COEP); National Innovation and Start-up Policy Cell (NISP); REDX AI Club; American Chemical Society Students' Chapter; Industry Advisory Board (IAB); ACS; DLLE; and Google Developer club.

provisions.text: The Student Council is selected to look after the welfare of students and to promote and co-ordinate the extracurricular activities of different student associations. The Council shall not engage in political activities. It consists of: Principal (Chairman); Dean-Student Welfare; National Service Scheme Programme Officer; one student from each class nominated by the Principal; Sports Incharge; General Secretary (nominated from students); Cultural Secretary (nominated from students); Sports Secretary (nominated from students); NSS Head; and two Lady Representatives (nominated from students).

provisions.topic: how to join a cell or club
provisions.text: Every cell or club has one or more faculty coordinators depending on requirement. Cells and clubs with student members constitute their members every year. A notice is sent to all students in the college regarding the election process for various cells and clubs, and student members also publicize the selection process. Every cell or club asks students to fill their respective forms and indicate their interest in holding different posts. Interviews are held after short listing, various posts are assigned by the concerned coordinators, and the final list is prepared and submitted to the Students' Welfare committee.

In cells like NISP, IIC and DLLE which work as per the guidance of central bodies and universities, the Principal nominates the Faculty Coordinator and some faculty members from different branches for assistance. The selection process for student members is the same as for other cells and clubs.

The Sports Committee consists of a Sports Incharge (a senior faculty member), one faculty member from each department, one representative from non-teaching staff and the Sports Secretary from the Student Council. Its duties are to prepare the schedule for sports activities on campus; conduct indoor and outdoor intra-collegiate tournaments; organize the institute Sports Festival, SCORE; identify sports talent and select teams for various games; and encourage and help students to participate in intercollegiate, state level and national level tournaments.

The Cultural Committee consists of a Cultural Incharge (a senior faculty member), one faculty member from each department, one representative from non-teaching staff and the Cultural Secretary from the Student Council. It organizes activities during the cultural festival SURGE and throughout the year, and encourages students to participate in intercollegiate, state and national level activities.

The Technical Committee is constituted to look after the organization of various technical events. It leads ISTE, IEEE, IET, IEI and other professional bodies to organize the technical festival of the institute, RENAISSANCE. It consists of a Coordinator (a senior faculty member) and one faculty member from each department.

The Industrial Visit Committee has the Principal as Convener, a senior faculty as Coordinator and one senior faculty of each branch as members. Its duties include deciding rules and regulations for industrial visits, arranging industrial visits frequently, and inviting people from industry for guest lectures. One day or two or more day industrial visits can be planned at institute level and executed only after the permission of the Industrial Visit Committee.
provisions.ambiguity: The rules and regulations for industrial visits are delegated to this committee and are NOT SPECIFIED IN SOURCE.

provisions.text: The National Service Scheme (NSS) is an aided extra-curricular activity conducted by the University of Mumbai and the Department of Youth Affairs and Sports, Government of India. Its motto is 'NOT ME BUT YOU'. The NSS team is led by an NSS Coordinator with one faculty member from each department, and undertakes activities like tree plantation, blood donation camps, disaster management, national integration camps, immunization and adventure programs.

The Magazine Committee provides a platform for students and teaching and non-teaching staff to show their literary talent in Marathi, Gujarati, Hindi and English. It is responsible for preparing the college newsletter and publishing the college magazine AURA every year. It consists of one teaching faculty of Communication Skills as coordinator, one faculty from each department, student coordinators for each language and a student coordinator for design work. Members scrutinize articles collected from students and staff, and selected articles are published.

The Green Club follows the Green policy of the institute, which refers to the organization's commitment towards environmental issues like air and water pollution, waste management, ecosystem management and protection and preservation of natural resources. Guidelines include communication of environmental issues through awareness programs (waste management, cleanliness, woman health, yoga, aerobics); social dimension for quality of life and health; plantation drives on and off campus; segregation of waste and waste management; implementation of a Waste to Wealth project producing manure from canteen and garden waste; purchase of green products; and recycling of e-waste by an authorized agency. The Green Club is headed by a senior faculty and anyone who wishes to work on environmental issues can join.

The Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) Cell is constituted under the leadership of the Principal, with the Dean-Research and Development and HODs of all departments as members. The IPR cell prepares the IPR Policy. The Intellectual Property Policy of the Institute governs all decisions and actions concerning the generation, handling, protection and commercialization of Intellectual Property.
provisions.ambiguity: The IPR Policy itself is NOT published in this handbook - only the cell that prepares it.

provisions.text: The Institute's Innovation Council (IIC), started in 2018 under the guidelines of the Ministry of Education's Innovation Cell (MIC), promotes innovation and entrepreneurship at institute level. Its functions include conducting innovation and entrepreneurship activities prescribed by MIC; mentoring, identifying and rewarding innovations and sharing success stories; organizing innovation-oriented workshops, seminars and interactions with entrepreneurs, investors and professionals and creating a mentor pool for student innovators; highlighting innovative projects by faculty and students; and organizing idea competitions, business plan competitions, mini-challenges and hackathons.

provisions.topic: national innovation and startup policy cell
provisions.text: The National Innovation and Start-up Policy 2019 for students and faculty of Higher Education Institutions enables institutes to engage students, staff and faculty in innovation and entrepreneurship activities. As per guidelines given by the Assistant Innovation Director at the Ministry of Education's Innovation Cell and AICTE in an online session on 11 January 2021, a committee was formed for the implementation and monitoring of NISP at KJSIEIT.

K J Somaiya Institute of Engineering and Information Technology, Sion has been registered with DLLE, the Department of Lifelong Learning and Extension, University of Mumbai, during Academic Year 2019-20. An opportunity is open to students to gain 10 marks grace at the Final Exam during every year provided they work for 120/240 hours of extension activities or projects.

policies.name: Internal Grievance / Complaint Cell
policies.purpose: To develop a responsive and accountable attitude among all stakeholders in order to maintain a harmonious educational atmosphere in the institute.
policies.scope: Complaints received from any student or staff of the College.

provisions.text: The Internal Grievance Cell / Redressal Cell has the Principal as Chairman, five teaching staff (one from each department), one HOD and one Registrar as members. The cell has the provision of being reconstituted every five years.

numbers.of: teaching members of the grievance cell

provisions.text: The college has its own Internal Grievance / Complaint Cell under direct supervision of the Principal. Anyone with a genuine grievance may approach the department members in person, or any member of the cell. If the person is unwilling to appear in person, grievances may be dropped in writing at the letterbox or suggestion box of the Grievance Cell at the Administrative Blocks, the Entrance and in the Canteen.

An applicant shall submit the application of grievance or appeal to a member of the Internal Grievance / Complaint Cell THROUGH THE HEAD OF DEPARTMENT. After verifying the facts the committee will try to redress the grievance within a reasonable time. While dealing with the complaint the committee at all levels will hear the complainant of the concerned people, and the relevant provisions of the Act or Regulations are kept in mind.
provisions.ambiguity: 'Within a reasonable time' is not quantified; there is no stated grievance redressal SLA.

provisions.text: If the applicant is not satisfied with the solution of the Committee, then the student can go to the University level Redressal Grievance Cell.

Cases are attended promptly on receipt of written grievances. The cell formally reviews all cases and acts as per Management policy. The cell reports to the Principal about cases attended and pending cases requiring direction from higher authorities. Members are empowered to sort out problems at their level through discussion with the applicant. Considering the nature and depth of the grievance, due inquiry is made by the members and the matter is solved through personal discussion. If anybody is found guilty of any kind of nuisance, the redressal is carried out with due consideration with the Principal.

The nature of action for redressal includes imposing a fine, issuing a memo, expelling from the college as per the rule of the institute and management, and informing the police if the situation so arises.
provisions.ambiguity: Fine amounts are NOT SPECIFIED IN SOURCE.

provisions.text: The final responsibility for grievance redressal rests with the Committee constituted by the Principal of the college. Grievance redressal should be time bound and result oriented, and the cell shall furnish a report on grievance redressal status and position to the Principal.
