provisions.text: The All India Council for Technical Education, New Delhi has issued a Notification dated 01-07-2009 for Prevention and Prohibition of Ragging in technical institutions, universities including deemed-to-be universities imparting technical education. The institute will follow all the Regulations for Prevention and Prohibition of Ragging.

The institute shall constitute an Anti-Ragging Committee nominated and headed by the Head of the Institution, consisting of representatives of civil and police administration, local media, Non Government Organizations involved in youth activities, representatives of faculty members, representatives of parents, representatives of students belonging to the freshers category as well as senior students, and non-teaching staff, with a diverse mix of membership in terms of level as well as gender.

Ragging complaints will be handled by the Anti-Ragging Committee as per government guidelines. Recommendations of this committee will be forwarded to the Principal for final decision. All employees of the Institute have to cooperate to the fullest possible manner in any internal investigation conducted by this committee.
provisions.ambiguity: The specific punishments for ragging are not enumerated in the handbook; it defers to AICTE regulations and government guidelines.

provisions.text: The Anti Ragging Squad is constituted as per AICTE guidelines with one senior faculty as chairman and one faculty from each department as a member. The squad takes regular rounds in the premises to prevent any ragging activity, counsels newly admitted students and advises them to approach the concerned Anti-Ragging Committee members if they experience any type of ragging activity.
Newly admitted students must submit an online anti-ragging affidavit available on the AICTE website; a printout of this affidavit is collected and maintained by the Student Section.

policies.name: College Women Development Cell (CWDC)
policies.purpose: To implement the directions of the University Women Development Cell and to deal with complaints and cases of sexual harassment in relation to the college.
policies.scope: As per the guideline given by the University of Mumbai. The office of the CWDC is located in the college and the Principal is the custodian of all records of the cell.

provisions.text: The Principal of the college is ex-officio President of the Cell. Members are two from the teaching staff, at least one of whom shall be a woman and the convener of the cell, nominated by the Principal; one woman member from the non-teaching staff; one woman representative from an NGO; one member from the reserved category; and one representative from the students' council (LR) nominated by the Principal. Not less than half the members of the CWDC shall be women.

numbers.of: minimum share of women members on the CWDC

provisions.text: The CWDC ensures implementation of University Women Development Cell (UWDC) Directions; processes all individual complaints concerning sexual harassment received from any person and takes suitable action as per the directives; deputes members to attend UWDC workshops and training programs; implements programs to spread awareness of these Directions; distributes UWDC publications among teachers, non-teaching employees and students; and exercises such other powers and functions as may be conferred on it.

provisions.topic: complaint against the principal or management
provisions.text: In case of a complaint against the Principal or a Member of the Management, the CWDC shall direct the complainant to approach the UWDC for redressal of grievances.

The term of office of the CWDC is 3 years except the student member, who is nominated every academic year. The names and contact numbers of members should be displayed on the college notice board. A person is disqualified from being nominated or continuing as a member if there is any complaint concerning moral turpitude, criminal proceedings pending in a court of law, or if found guilty of sexual harassment. A member absent for three consecutive meetings without the President's permission vacates office. The CWDC shall meet at least twice every academic year and the interval between two meetings shall not exceed six months.

provisions.section: 4.17.3 Procedure for investigation of complaints (2018 edition)
provisions.text: The CWDC acts as Complaint Committee, excluding the student member. Any woman employee or female student has the right to lodge a complaint with any CWDC member concerning sexual harassment, molestation or misbehaviour. A complaint may be oral or in writing duly signed by the complainant; an oral complaint is reduced to writing in detail by the member and is not acted upon until signed by the complainant. A confidential complaint register is maintained. The member receiving the complaint reports to the convener within ten working days; if the complainant desires, her name is kept confidential and not divulged even to the CWDC. Within two weeks the convener convenes a CWDC meeting where the complainant or her representative is heard; if she specifically desires to depose before only women members she shall be allowed to, though male members still participate in the decision making. If the complainant wishes that a warning would suffice, the alleged offender is called, heard and may be warned, and the matter is concluded with a recording in the Complaint Register. If the complainant wishes to proceed beyond a warning, the CWDC asks for a written explanation and may proceed with an enquiry, making a suitable recommendation to the Principal or Management. The CWDC affords fair and reasonable opportunity to the delinquent to defend and ensures the principles of natural justice.

numbers.of: deadline for the member to report to the convener
deadline to convene a CWDC meeting

provisions.text: If the complainant feels there is a delay on the part of the college authorities in processing the case, the complainant can approach the CWDC of the University directly after six weeks of registering the complaint. After a preliminary inquiry, if the CWDC concludes that the case merits further enquiry, it refers the case to the UWDC and hands over all requisite documents with its findings within a month of the receipt of the complaint.

numbers.of: time after which the complainant may approach the University CWDC directly
deadline to refer a case to the UWDC

provisions.text: An employee found guilty of sexual harassment is liable to receive Minor Penalties - warning, reprimand or censure; fine; withholding of increments or promotion; reduction to a post in the lower pay scale or to a lower stage of increment - or Major Penalties - compulsory retirement; termination of service; removal or dismissal from service.

A student found guilty of sexual harassment is liable to receive Minor Penalties - warning; written apology; bond of good behavior; debarring entry into hostel or campus; suspension for a specified period of time; withholding results - or Major Penalties - debarring from examinations; expulsion from college.

If the complainant is a student and the accused a teacher, during the pendency of the investigation and enquiry and even after, if the teacher is found guilty, the accused shall not act as an examiner for any examination for which the student appears. If the complainant and the accused are both employees, during the pendency and even after, if the accused is found guilty, the accused shall not write the Confidential Report of the complainant. In case of sexual harassment on college premises, active assistance shall be provided to the complainant by the college to pursue the complaint and the safety of the complainant shall be ensured.

policies.name: Information Communication Technology (IT) Policies
policies.purpose: Policies covering web-based applications, connectivity, hardware and software, Wi-Fi, capital purchase, equipment scrap, internet use, domain controller, software licensing, ERP and e-learning.

provisions.text: Somaiya Vidyavihar provides faculty, staff and students a variety of computing resources and online services. An SVVNetID - an account name identifying you as a member of the Somaiya Vidyavihar community - and password is required to access most of these services (OPAC access, access to SVV campus computer/laptop, access to the SVV AD Portal, applying for railway travel concession, and wired and Wi-Fi internet access). When a student or staff member is admitted to KJSIEIT, the SVVNetID is created automatically and the SVVNetID and password are supplied to their Somaiya Email ID and personal mobile. Access to specific online services is determined by eligibility and authority. The account is managed at http://myaccount.somaiya.edu, where members can manage personal information displayed in the SVV database, change the password for SVV services and reset a forgotten password.

The Somaiya Email id is given by the Somaiya Institute to all students, staff and faculty. FOR STUDENTS IT IS A LIFETIME EMAIL ID. The access link is mail.somaiya.edu. Anyone who does not know their Somaiya email id can contact the Google Apps Coordinator of their institute. Every Google Apps coordinator has rights to reset the password for a Somaiya email id using the student's Member id, which is on the RFID card. Somaiya members can also reset the password through the SVV NETID portal; once reset, the system sends a new password to the personal email id and an SMS to the mobile.

Google Apps is a set of web applications provided by Google including Google Email, Google Calendar, Google Docs, Google Talk (Chat), Google Mobile and Google Sites, offering an online alternative to traditional office suites. Staff and students are expected to use Google Apps efficiently, and Google Coordinators train new users and keep them up to date.
Book circulation, reservation, reminders and book and journal search facilities are managed by Bookworm Software, with a link made available at http://114.143.198.3/opac.

provisions.section: 11.1.5 KJSIEIT Website Portal Updating and Maintenance
provisions.text: Institute and departmental activities, notices, events, circulars and photos need to be displayed on the website, which must be updated and maintained regularly. Institute and department level data should be provided regularly to the website administrator by the HOD or Website coordinator, and online event registration details must be provided well in advance.

To get a new ID card if the ID card is LOST: immediately report to the Institute's Office with a written application; get an FIR from the nearest Police Station where the card was lost; pay the fee to replace a lost ID card at the institute's office before a new ID Card is issued; the ID Card coordinator at the institute office generates a ticket against the lost ID card; once the ticket is generated, approach the ID Card office to get the new ID card and collect it within 2 working days from the date of ticket generation.

numbers.of: time to collect a replacement ID card

provisions.ambiguity: The ID card replacement fee amount is NOT SPECIFIED IN SOURCE.

provisions.text: To get a new ID card if the ID card is damaged or the chip is not working: immediately report to the Institute's Office with a written application; pay the replacement fee at the institute's office; the ID Card coordinator generates a ticket against the damaged ID card; approach the ID Card office and collect the new card within 2 working days from ticket generation. The old ID card must be returned for a replacement. Note: in case of problems with the ID card chip, first visit the ID card office, where staff will do the necessary checking and certify the chip damage.

numbers.of: time to collect a replacement ID card

provisions.text: To get a new lanyard or card holder: pay the replacement fee at the institute office; the ID Card coordinator generates a new ticket against the lanyard or card holder; approach the ID Card office and collect the material within 2 working days from ticket generation.

numbers.of: time to collect a replacement lanyard

provisions.text: Online feedback conduction software should be developed in house. Online feedback should be conducted twice a semester. The report should be generated by software mapping to NBA faculty assessment. Evaluation of feedback should be used for improvement of faculty performance, and improved faculty performance should be mapped with the upcoming feedback by software.
As an alternative to the existing internet leased line, broadband and Wi-Fi internet connections are necessary as a standby provision which must be in active condition.

Install only licensed copies of software, and licensed copies must be updated. The computer name, asset number, specifications and installed licensed software must be displayed on the CPU. An asset register, consumable register and history card should be maintained and updated with equipment spares, repairing details and software changes for each lab. History cards must be verified and signed by lab in-charges every month and by the HOD every semester. Documents for computers, peripherals, spares and repairs purchased must be preserved.

numbers.of: history card verification by lab in-charge

provisions.text: Wi-Fi facility is made available on the campus FOR AUTHENTICATED USERS ONLY. For campus Wi-Fi access an internal user should use the SVV NetID and password allotted to them. For external users, guest access should be provided. Wi-Fi security policies can be set using a firewall.

All capital items should be purchased only by the Purchase Committee of the Institute. Any department desiring to purchase a capital item must submit the proposal in the prescribed format to the purchase department, which verifies the available budget and valid need. Before submitting the proposal, the indenter in consultation with the Purchase Committee establishes the requirement. On verification the Principal grants financial sanction. No capital expenditure, irrespective of its value, can be incurred without prior sanction from Head Office.

Staff of KJSIEIT must use the internet facility only for official and academic purposes; must not send unsolicited mails through the KJSIEIT internet facility; must not download material from the internet without proper acknowledgement of the original source; and must not watch unsolicited videos or waste internet resources. Guest login should be made available for external authorized participants.
provisions.ambiguity: The Internet Facility Policy is written for STAFF only. No equivalent acceptable-use rule for students' internet use is stated, other than the digital library rules in the Library Manual.

provisions.text: Windows OS computers have to be connected in the SVV domain. Active Directory controller policies can be maintained by the network admin team.

Under Active Directory, only legally purchased licensed software can be used. To install legal licensed software, rights should be given to heads of respective departments only. After every legal licensed software installation HODs must ensure the password is changed to avoid further unauthorized access. The IT and network admin team of the institute must do vigilance randomly.

In-house ERP software can be developed by staff members as per institute requirements so that it can be modified as and when requirements change. Training and support must be provided to the staff using ERP software, and reports of ERP software should be available to staff members.

Every classroom and lab should have e-learning equipment setup availability. E-learning resource materials available at NPTEL and IITB should be verified by faculty as per curriculum requirements, and faculty should be able to add their expertise, knowledge and experience with e-learning material.

policies.name: Human Resource Policies (2018 edition)
policies.purpose: To assist the management to execute the HR policies consistently and transparently; to define the rules staff must abide by, the code of conduct and their responsibilities toward the institute; and to state staff rights and motivation policies.
policies.scope: All teaching, non-teaching and daily wages employees of KJSIEIT.

provisions.text: The Human Resource Policies chapter covers: 4.1 Introduction; 4.2 Objective; 4.3 Organizational Structure; 4.4 Duties and responsibilities of employees; 4.5 Manpower planning; 4.6 Recruitment of Teaching Staff; 4.7 Recruitment of Non-Teaching Staff; 4.8 Induction; 4.9 Training and Development of Teaching and Support Staff; 4.10 Salary Structure; 4.11 Performance Monitoring System; 4.12 Career Progression; 4.13 Code of Professional Ethics for a Teacher; 4.14 Employee Benefits; 4.15 Leave Policy; 4.16 Grievances handling; 4.17 College Women Development Committee; 4.18 Resignation Policy; 4.19 Exit Policy; 4.20 Retirement Policy; 4.21 List of Holidays; and Annexure II (Exit Interview Form).

Objectives of the HR policy: to assist the management to execute HR policies consistently and transparently; to define the rules that staff have to abide by, the code of conduct and their responsibilities toward the institute; and to state staff rights and motivation policies to encourage them to work to their best potential.

Additional incentives for publication in refereed journals are provided to faculty members: a journal having an impact factor above 3 earns Rs. 3,000 per publication; a journal having an impact factor between 2 and 3 earns Rs. 1,500 per publication.

numbers.of: incentive for impact factor between 2 and 3

provisions.text: Teaching and non-teaching staff appointed as regular employees are eligible for an annual increment as prescribed by rule subject to performance appraisal and ACR. Staff who availed Leave Without Pay beyond 15 days will not be eligible for the annual increment. Career Advancement Schemes for teaching staff are implemented as per AICTE norms and SVV policies and rules.

numbers.of: LWP threshold that forfeits the annual increment

provisions.text: For non-teaching staff, an appraisal form is filled each year by the respective HOD, then the Registrar and then the Principal, depending on punctuality, communication and work performance. Staff are eligible for annual increments according to their appraisal and can be promoted to the next level if a vacancy exists and they meet the eligibility criteria. If performance is extraordinary the final decision on extra increments and promotion is at the discretion of the Principal and management. If not promoted, the time scale of the higher post is given after 12 years of continuous service in the post without any adverse remark on the Academic Confidential Report.

numbers.of: continuous service after which the higher post time scale is given

provisions.topic: code of professional ethics for a teacher
provisions.section: 4.13 Code of Professional Ethics for a Teacher
provisions.text: Teachers should adhere to a responsible pattern of conduct and demeanour expected by the community; manage private affairs consistently with the dignity of the profession; seek continuous professional growth through study and research; express free and frank opinion at professional meetings, seminars and conferences; maintain active membership of professional organizations; perform teaching, tutorial, practical, seminar and research work conscientiously; and co-operate in the educational responsibilities of the college and university, including appraising admission applications, advising and counselling students, and assisting the conduct of examinations including supervision, invigilation and evaluation, and participating in extension, co-curricular and extra-curricular activities including community service.

Teachers should respect the right and dignity of the student in expressing his or her opinion; deal justly and impartially with students regardless of religion, caste, political, economic, social and physical characteristics; recognize differences in aptitude and capability and strive to meet individual needs; encourage students to improve their attainments and develop their personalities; inculcate scientific outlook and respect for physical labour and ideals of democracy, patriotism and peace; be affectionate to students and not behave vindictively towards any of them for any reason; pay attention only to the attainment of the student in the assessment of merit; make themselves available to students even beyond class hours and help and guide them without any remuneration or reward; aid students to develop an understanding of national heritage and goals; and refrain from inciting students against other students, colleagues or administration.

Teachers should refrain from undertaking any other employment and commitment including private tuitions and coaching classes which are likely to interfere with their professional responsibilities. They should adhere to the conditions of contract, give and expect due notice before a change of position, and refrain from availing leave except on unavoidable grounds and as far as practicable with prior intimation, keeping in view their responsibility for completion of the academic schedule.

All regular staff who have completed two years of continuous service are eligible for LTA, available to self, spouse and 2 children only. Those who have more than 2 children after 2000 are not eligible. Employees whose spouse works in the same or another organization and claims LTA from that employer are not eligible. Entitlements: all teachers, librarian and regular staff on consolidated salary of Rs 40,000 and above get 2 tier AC / First Class; regular staff with AGP/GP Rs 4,400 to Rs 5,600 or consolidated salary from Rs 30,001 up to Rs 40,000 get 3 tier AC; staff with GP Rs 4,200 to Rs 4,300 or consolidated salary of Rs 25,000 to Rs 30,000 get AC Chair car; all others get second class / sleeper class with ticket proof needed. The home town address is as recorded in the Service Book at the time of joining and can be changed only once during the entire service. Staff whose home town is not in Maharashtra are eligible up to 400 KM from the Maharashtra border. Staff claiming LTA must proceed on leave to be eligible for the claim.

numbers.of: continuous service required for LTA eligibility
eligibility limit beyond the Maharashtra border

provisions.text: Maharashtra Darshan is given only to non-teaching staff once in 4 years. In a block of four years staff may take either 2 LTA and no Maharashtra Darshan, or one LTA and Maharashtra Darshan.

As per University Circular No. Estb.II(IV)/EST/ICC/2012-13/21 of 2012 dated 13 September 2013, all non-teaching staff are covered under a Group Medical Insurance Policy. The premium for each staff member is paid by the Management up to Rs 3,500; any amount above that has to be contributed by the staff. Non-teaching staff who do not want cover beyond the statutory limit of Rs 3,500 may decline, in which case they are covered only up to a premium of Rs 3,500. This rule can be changed by the government and Management. This health insurance policy is only for non-teaching staff, though the same facility can be extended to teaching staff as well.

All teaching, non-teaching and daily wages staff are eligible for Provident Fund according to the statutory limits of 12% up to Rs 15,000, a maximum deduction of Rs 1,800, and the management contributes the same amount. It can be withdrawn or transferred to other institutes on resignation.

For all teaching, non-teaching and daily wages staff, gratuity is given at the time of leaving the Institute. All teaching, non-teaching and daily wages staff must complete 5 years of service to be eligible for gratuity. The Institute has taken a policy from LIC through which the amount is paid to the concerned staff.

At the time of leaving the Institute, employees must return all books to the library and any other issued material to the respective department; clear all dues regarding department, Accounts section and Institute; and submit a 'NO DUES' certificate from all departments, library, office and accounts section. After these formalities they must return the Identity Card issued at the time of joining. After NO DUES is submitted to Establishment it is forwarded to the Accounts Section, which prepares the dues such as leave salary, Provident Fund and Gratuity. A relieving letter is then issued to the employee.

Local conveyance for staff travelling within the city on official work: non-teaching staff on official visits to DTE/University travel by bus or local train at actual; non-teaching staff carrying heavy material or in an emergency travel by auto or taxi at actual; Faculty, Registrar and Principal on official work travel by auto or taxi at actual, or by own car at Rs. 9 per km.

Outstation conveyance: non-teaching staff travel by ordinary sleeper class or bus at actual; Faculty and Registrar by III AC at actual; Principal by II AC at actual; Faculty, Registrar and Principal by own car at Rs. 9 per km. Dearness Allowance is Rs. 300 per day in metro cities like Delhi, Kolkata, Pune, Chennai and Bangalore, and Rs. 200 per day for other cities. Lodging: non-teaching staff Rs. 1,000 per day in metro cities and Rs. 800 per day in other cities; Faculty and Registrar Rs. 1,500 per day in metro cities and Rs. 1,200 per day in other cities; Principal Rs. 2,000 per day in metro cities and Rs. 1,500 per day in other cities. Staff must clear all conveyance, DA and lodging claims within three days after completion of the tour and submit a report of the official work done to the HOD or Principal.

Before proceeding for any type of leave, any teaching staff, non-teaching staff, HOD or Head of Institution must mention on the application form itself the name of the person in-charge who will perform the duties on their behalf.

All employees are entitled to 8 days of Casual Leave during a calendar year (January to December) on a pro rata basis. CLs are used at the discretion of the employee, subject to the approval of the respective HOD and Principal. Unused CLs will NOT be carried over to the subsequent calendar year under any circumstances. Employees must apply for CL in the prescribed format. Not more than 3 CLs can be availed in continuation, and CL can be taken for half a day. Casual Leave cannot be prefixed or suffixed to vacation or any other type of leave, except On Duty leave.

Regular employees are eligible for 10 days of Sick Leave during a calendar year (January to December) on completion of one year of service. A written request (oral in exceptional cases) is required. An employee returning from sick leave must submit a medical certificate and a fitness certificate from a registered medical practitioner. In case of sudden illness the employee should notify the HOD immediately by phone, or a family member should inform the college authorities. Unused sick leave is carried forward into subsequent years and can be accumulated up to 300 days.

numbers.of: service required before sick leave eligibility

provisions.text: On Duty leave is granted to an employee when the University, Principal, HOD or any other competent authority assigns a duty that has to be carried out for the institute or University. The employee must fill the OD form and get it approved from the HOD.

All female employees who are regular employees and have completed two years of service are eligible for 180 days of maternity leave. Female employees who have completed one year but less than two years of continuous service are eligible for maternity leave on a pro-rata basis. Maternity Leave is available for two children only. Maternity leave can be availed by staff who have an abortion or MTP for a period up to 45 days, only after 2 months of confirmation of pregnancy, on producing medical certificates from a qualified doctor; this facility is allowed once in service.

numbers.of: service required for full maternity leave

provisions.text: All male employees are eligible for paternity leave of 7 days, up to 2 children only.

Non-teaching employees required to work extra hours or on holidays are eligible for compensatory off at the rate of hours worked. Teaching staff required to work on holidays are eligible for compensatory off equivalent to the days worked, which can be availed at any time except when regular teaching is in progress. Compensatory off can be prefixed or suffixed with any type of leave and should be availed during the calendar year and not carried forward, though in special circumstances it can be accumulated and carried forward.

Teaching staff, the Training & Placement Officer, Technical Support Staff and the Librarian are entitled to vacation and are called vacational staff. The Principal, Registrar and all other non-teaching staff are non-vacational staff. The number of vacation days is decided by the Management (Principal) as per norms and the academic calendar, totalling 70 days vacation - 30 days winter vacation and 40 days summer vacation - during an academic year. Eligibility to avail vacation is for staff on regular appointment, entitled to full vacation on completion of one year of service. Ad-hoc staff are not eligible for vacation.

Staff should be present on the last working day prior to proceeding on vacation and should report on duty on the first working day after their vacation. Staff remaining absent on ANY ONE of these days will have 15 days salary deducted; staff remaining absent on BOTH days will have 30 days salary deducted. In exceptional cases, a staff member absent on medical grounds must submit a medical certificate from a qualified doctor or Somaiya Hospital on the very first day of resuming duty; sanctioning is at the discretion of the Principal.

numbers.of: deduction for absence on one of the two days
deduction for absence on both days

provisions.text: Vacational staff during their vacation can be recalled for official work or examination work, whatever the nature; failing to report is treated as misconduct. The recalled staff is eligible for Earned Leave at the ratio 1:2.3 (one Earned Leave = 2.3 vacation days).

numbers.of: conversion ratio for recalled vacational staff

provisions.text: Earned Leave applies only to regular staff. Non-vacational regular staff are entitled to 30 days Earned Leave on completion of one year of service, January to December, on a pro-rata basis. Earned leave can be accumulated up to 300 days for regular staff. Not more than 120 days of Earned Leave will be granted in a stretch except on medical grounds.

numbers.of: earned leave entitlement for non-vacational regular staff
maximum earned leave in a stretch

provisions.text: An employee wishing to resign should inform the Head of Department and tender the resignation in writing to the Principal, clearly stating the date from which the resignation becomes effective, bearing in mind the contractual notice period, and mentioning the reason for resignation. The employee appears for the exit interview. In case of an ad-hoc appointment the employee must give a minimum of thirty days written notice unless a shorter period is acceptable to the Head of Department; for a regular employee the notice period is three months.

An employee leaving without serving the notice period will not receive their pay for, or will have to deposit salary for, the notice period. Employees interested in resigning cannot utilize any leave except On Duty and Compensatory Off. An employee who resigns during an academic semester is released after the academic session keeping in mind the interest of the students, or may be released only in exceptional cases.

All employees who have resigned should hand over charge to the appropriate person in consultation with the Head of Department and inform the Principal. The employee must submit a 'No Dues Certificate' from all departments on or before the last day of work, and will be relieved only after submitting it.

The exit interview of a resigned employee is conducted by the Head of Department and the Principal. After a one-to-one discussion, the HOD or Principal fills the Exit Interview Form in the prescribed format (Annexure II). The purpose is to find the exact reason for resignation and suggest remedial measures to management to reduce future attrition; an attempt should be made to get real, frank and free feedback. The form records name, designation, date of joining, reason for resignation as told by the employee, name of the new employer, salary offered by the new employer, positives and negatives in the environment and employment conditions of KJSIEIT, reason for resignation as understood by the interviewer, whether the employee would be re-employed in future, and any other feedback.

The retirement policy applies to both teaching and non-teaching staff. For teaching faculty the retirement age is 60 years, and after retirement the faculty can be continued if the Management wants. For non-teaching staff the retirement age is 58 for Class III and 60 years for Class IV, and staff can be continued if the Management wants.

numbers.of: retirement age for teaching faculty and Class IV non-teaching staff
retirement age for Class III non-teaching staff

provisions.text: Holiday is given as per the University Circulars and Management.
provisions.ambiguity: NOT SPECIFIED IN SOURCE: no actual holiday list or number of holidays is published in the handbook; it defers entirely to University circulars and Management.

provisions.text: The Institute recognizes the right of employees and students to express their grievances and seek a solution concerning disagreements arising from working relationships, working conditions, employment practices or differences of interpretation of policy. A suggestion-cum-complaint box is kept in the college canteen in which students and staff can put their grievances in writing, and grievances can be lodged personally to any member of the Grievance committee. Two committees are established: the General Grievances Committee, constituted to help employees, students and parents record complaints and get problems related to academics, resources and personal grievances solved; and the Anti-Ragging Committee, which handles ragging complaints as per government guidelines. Recommendations of these committees are forwarded to the Principal for final decision, and all employees must cooperate fully in any internal investigation.

policies.name: Revised Higher Studies Policy - PhD Sponsorship and Study Leave
policies.purpose: Rules and regulations for KJSIEIT faculty who want to pursue a PhD at UGC-recognized and AICTE-approved institutes affiliated to universities, including sponsorship categories, study leave, bonds, penalties and incentives.
policies.scope: KJSIEIT teaching staff. References: SVV Higher Studies Policy 2012 and KJSCE revised higher study policy 2012-13. Signed by Dr. Suresh K. Ukarande (Principal, KJSIEIT), Dr. Preeti Rawat (Director HR, SVV, Somaiya Ayurvihar) and Dr. Rajasekaran Pillai (Provost, Somaiya Vidyavihar), dated 22/12/21, institute inward number 193 dated 31/12/2021.
policies.source_format_note: These 15 pages are SCANNED IMAGES with no extractable text layer; they were read visually page by page.

provisions.section: I) Applying for the PhD selection procedure
provisions.text: Sponsorship cannot be claimed as a matter of right but is the prerogative of KJSIEIT. Faculty must have completed the probation period and previous agreement period, if any. Faculty has to apply to the Principal, through the HOD, requesting submission of the application to respective universities, 6 months prior to the PhD interview, selection or application submission, whichever is earlier. The application period should be strictly between January and June for November/December PhD processing, and between July and December for January-June PhD processing, of every year.

numbers.of: lead time before the PhD interview or application to apply to the Principal

provisions.text: All received applications are scrutinized against: total years of experience; total number of publications; total number of minor/major research grants; API index for the last 3 self-appraisals; contribution to institute R&D activity; contribution to institute development initiatives; contribution to outside and institute level project development; and R&D score of the last 3 self-appraisals. Candidates scoring more than 50% on these criteria undergo an interview with the Planning and Evaluation Committee of KJSIEIT. On approval from the Planning and Evaluation Committee, the candidate may be permitted to proceed for PhD application.

numbers.of: minimum score on the scrutiny criteria to reach interview

provisions.section: II) Criterion for Sponsoring PhD Program
provisions.text: A maximum of 01 faculty per division per department will be sponsored for PhD per year: 02 faculties for a 120 intake and 01 faculty for a 60 intake.

numbers.unit: faculty per division per department per year

numbers.of: sponsorship quota for a department with 120 intake

provisions.text: Category 1: faculty who secure admission through the Quality Improvement Program (QIP) in reputed national level institutes like IITs, NITs or IISc can avail 3 years fully paid Study Leave. For Category 1, 70% of the regular gross salary (excluding TA) is paid for the 3 years of fully relieved study leave.

numbers.of: share of regular gross salary paid during fully relieved study leave

provisions.text: Category 2: faculty who secure admission through QIP in Government or Government-aided organizations like VJTI or COEP get fully paid study leave for completion of course work or thesis writing for 6 months or 1 year as required by the organization; in addition they can avail 1 day per week leave for the next 2.5 or 2 years of the total 3 year study leave, typically for the 15 week term of the University i.e. 30 days a year. Category 3: faculty who secure admission through the PhD entrance test (PET) at various universities in reputed institutes get fully paid study leave for completion of course work or thesis writing for 6 months, plus 1 day per week leave for the next 2.5 years of the 3 year study leave, again 15 weeks per term i.e. 30 days a year. For Categories 2 and 3, 70% of regular gross salary (excluding TA) is paid for the 6 month or 1 year fully relieved study leave.

numbers.of: university term length used to compute weekly study leave
gross salary during fully relieved leave

provisions.text: Category 4: faculty who secure admission at various institutes or universities through PET can avail 1 day per week Study Leave for a 3 year duration for completion of their PhD work, typically for the 15 week term of the University i.e. 30 days a year.

Category 5: faculty who secure PhD admission at research centres under University of Mumbai and/or Somaiya Vidyavihar University through the respective PETs and who do not want to avail any kind of study leave or other support facility, and are ready to handle all institute level responsibilities as a regular teacher. For Category 5 no study leave or other support facility is availed. Category 5 faculty select PhD research centres or universities around the Mumbai region only, so that they can report to PhD work on non-working days.
For all Category 1 to 4 study leaves, the relieving period will start from 1st July or 1st January of the respective academic year.

For Categories 2 and 3, 20 days additional vacation per year is given for the remaining 2.5 or 2 years of the total 3 years of study leave duration, typically 10 days in summer and 10 days in winter vacation. For Category 4, 20 days additional vacation per year is given for the 3 year study leave duration, typically 10 days in summer and 10 days in winter.

numbers.of: additional vacation in summer and in winter

provisions.text: Every faculty proceeding on study leave of the Institute is required to execute a Bond in the format given by KJSIEIT. NO FACULTY SHALL BE ALLOWED TO PROCEED ON STUDY LEAVE OR PURSUE PhD WITHOUT EXECUTING A BOND. Faculty need to sign a bond under any one category from 1 to 5. No faculty of the institute will pursue a PhD without the permission process mentioned in the 'Revised Higher Studies Policy of KJSIEIT'. Faculty pursuing a PhD without the permission of the institute shall not be considered eligible for any further benefits given to PhD candidates from the institute.

For Categories 2, 3, 4 and 5, for the remaining period and additional facility (1 day study leave per week and additional 20 days vacation duration), 83% of the regular gross salary will be paid to the faculty for the study leave duration.

numbers.of: gross salary during the partial study leave period

provisions.text: It is mandatory for all faculty sponsored under Categories 1 to 5 to publish their PhD work while doing the PhD in at least 2 Scopus/SCI indexed journals, and to file a patent and apply for various research grants.

Sponsored faculty under all 1 to 5 categories must submit to the Principal their half yearly progress report and Annual Progress Seminar (APS) report about the PhD study, duly signed by the respective Guide, HOD and Institute Authorities, without fail. Such reports shall be submitted to the Principal within 30 days on expiry of each 6 months of the study leave. The Institute may terminate the PhD Bond and Agreement on account of a breach of this clause, and the decision of the Institute shall remain final.

numbers.of: deadline to submit the progress report after each 6-month period

provisions.text: If the faculty fails to complete the PhD within six years from the date of relieving from the institute, registration or enrollment, or before completing 55 years of age whichever is earlier, or discontinues the PhD, the salary paid during fully relieved study leave, 1 day per week study leave duration and 20 days additional vacation per year duration shall be recovered in 12 equal monthly installments from notice of the case.

numbers.of: maximum time to complete the PhD

provisions.text: Candidates will not earn any Casual Leave, Sick Leave or vacation for the study leave duration. During the sponsorship period the Employee will not be allowed to avail Earned Leave.

On acquiring the PhD and on receipt of the PhD degree verification from the respective university, an incentive is given per year on a five year regular installment basis, in the month in which the PhD degree verification is received by the parent institute. Incentive money: 30% of the regular gross salary paid during the 3 years study leave for Category 1 and the 6 months or 1 year study leave for Categories 2 and 3; and 17% of the regular gross salary paid for study leave for Categories 2, 3 and 4 respectively for availing the additional facility of 1 day study leave and additional 20 days vacation duration.

numbers.of: incentive on fully relieved study leave salary
incentive on partial study leave salary

provisions.text: Percentage of incentive money given for serving the Institute after acquiring the PhD degree: on completion of the first year 20%; second year 20%; third year 20%; fourth year 20%; fifth year 20%.

numbers.of: incentive released each year for five years

provisions.text: Category 1 Agreement (3 yrs fully paid study leave for IITs/NITs/IISc): the Institute grants study leave up to a maximum of three years with full pay to enable the Employee to carry out research work without attending duties. The employee is not entitled to the usual annual increment during the period of sponsorship, nor to any type of leave or vacation during the study leave. Study Leave is neither an entitlement of the Employee nor obligatory on the part of the Management to grant. The candidate relieved under this category reports back to the Institute after completing 3 years of PhD work from the date of registration, admission, payment of fees or selection for the PhD, whichever is earlier. The study leave shall not be extended in any circumstances; however in exceptional cases the Institute may extend the period for acquiring the PhD for an additional period in without-pay mode at its sole discretion. The Employee shall continue in the service of the Institute as a member of the teaching staff for a minimum period of FIVE years from the date of acquiring the PhD degree or degree verification by the PhD granting University, whichever is later. The PhD study leave should be availed from 1st July or 1st January of the respective academic year.

numbers.of: minimum service bond after acquiring the PhD

provisions.text: If the Employee fails to acquire the PhD Degree within 5 years from the date of grant of study leave, and/or commits a breach of Clause 4, or abandons their studies, or leaves the services of the Institute within 5 years from acquiring the PhD, he or she shall pay back to the Institute the whole of the payment made by way of salary or emoluments during the period of study leave, along with penal interest at 14% compoundable quarterly till realization, PLUS a lump sum of Rs 5,00,000 (INR five lakh), and/or it will be recovered in 12 equal monthly installments from notice or realization of the case.

numbers.of: deadline to acquire the PhD and minimum post-PhD service

provisions.text: The PhD bond requires two Guarantors from the Institute (Guarantor No. 1 and Guarantor No. 2), who jointly and severally guarantee that the Employee will perform and observe all conditions of the Agreement and shall at all times pay to the Institute on demand all losses, costs, damages and expenses occasioned by the breach, non-performance or non-observance by the Employee. The Guarantors waive all objections and remedies including under the Limitation Act, 1963. If the employee fails to acquire the PhD within 5 years, abandons studies, does not join duties in 3 years, or the agreement is terminated for breach, the Guarantors shall jointly or severally pay KJSIEIT on demand all expenses of salary or emoluments of the employee along with the penalty.

numbers.of: guarantors required on the PhD bond

provisions.section: Category 2 & 3 Agreement clause 16 / Category 4 clause 11 / Category 5 clause 13
provisions.text: For Categories 2, 3, 4 and 5 the Employee must serve the Institute for a minimum period of FIVE years after acquiring the PhD Degree. On default, the salary paid during study leave and the 20 days additional vacation period shall be recovered in a lump along with interest at 14% compoundable quarterly from the date of payment till realization, PLUS a lump sum of Rs. 1,00,000 (Rupees One Lakh) as penalty, and/or recovered in 12 equal monthly installments from notice or realization of the case. For Category 5, if the Employee fails to complete the PhD within six years from registration or enrollment or before attaining 55 years of age, whichever is earlier, or discontinues, a lump sum of Rs. 1,00,000 will be charged as a penalty.

numbers.of: lump sum penalty under Categories 2 to 5

provisions.text: Category 5 (Somaiya Vidyavihar University and/or University of Mumbai research centres): the Institute grants permission and a No Objection Certificate to pursue the PhD for the maximum period prescribed by the respective university or a maximum of five years, whichever is less. The permission is effective from the date of registration, enrolment, or admission and payment of fees, or the date of signing the bond, whichever is later, and is granted from 1st July or 1st January of the respective academic year only. An Employee availing this facility shall NOT be eligible for any kind of study leave, office duty leave, oral permission leave from HOD or Principal, or any other support facility. The Employee handles all department, institute, trust and university level responsibilities as a regular teacher for the complete duration of the PhD work, and the total workload and all other duties remain unchanged. The Employee shall maintain quality academics and shall not remain absent, apply for leaves, or avoid, ignore or delay assigned duties in the term duration under the name of PhD work. The Employee is eligible for all other facilities as a regular teacher including casual, sick and vacation leave as per the rules of the institute. An Employee availing PhD sponsorship under this category is entitled to their regular salary as per rules.

Notwithstanding anything contained in the Agreement, the Institute may withdraw any concessions allowed payable to the Employee at any time without assigning any reason, and may terminate the Agreement or cancel its permission and No Objection for the PhD at any time without assigning any reason at its discretion. The Employee shall not be entitled to any compensation, concession, loss or claim for damages on account of termination, and gives a waiver on their part in this behalf. The Institute may also recall the Employee, cancelling the study leave, at any time without assigning any reason, and the Employee shall forthwith join the Institute.

policies.name: Quality Management System and IQAC
policies.purpose: Quality management and accreditation, including the constitution and functions of the Internal Quality Assurance Cell and the experiential learning initiative.

provisions.text: The Principal appoints an Internal Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC) which looks after quality management issues. The IQAC consists of an Accreditation coordinator who oversees preparations for accreditation under the guidance of the Principal, a secretary for documentation and coordination, and a program coordinator for each department. The Accreditation coordinator, program coordinators, Heads of departments and Deans, under the guidance of the Principal, work together to obtain accreditation. Facilitators are identified to create awareness and impart training to faculty, staff and students, and the committee organizes awareness workshops on the accreditation process.

The IQAC conducts a strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and challenges (SWOC) analysis preferably on NAAC/NBA criteria; identifies and analyzes issues and challenges to design strategies to achieve quality goals; assesses the performance of the programmes on NAAC/NBA criteria and ensures they get an A grade before starting preparation for accreditation, otherwise preparing an action plan to improve where they scored less; maintains significant and direct documents usable as evidence for quality; crafts achievable and realistic mission and vision statements for the Institute with department visions aligned to the Institute's; documents and publicizes best practices; maintains a policy document stating policies related to admission, recruitment, career advancement, purchase, placement, rewards and incentives, training and development, finance, safety, consultancy, industrial interaction, use of resources, use of information technology, preventing ragging, empowerment of women, encouraging physically challenged students and academic processes; ensures the academic and department calendars include industrial training, guidance and counselling, project, laboratory work and research plans; and prepares the library manual, placement manual and guidelines for industrial visits.

The Experiential Learning Initiative is a program of participation in activities promoting professionalism, lifelong learning and commitment to community and the profession, seeking to leverage local resources and integrate the community in education inside and outside the classroom. All students are strongly encouraged to take advantage of experiential learning opportunities throughout their College career. Project-Based Learning intensive workshops are organized; project-based initiatives include classroom projects across disciplines, mini-projects for second year students and community-based projects. An Experimental Learning Committee comprising dedicated students and faculty should be formulated, departments should develop plans including an assessment component for enhancing community involvement, and a funding plan should be developed identifying the appropriate level of base funding for community engagement and experiential learning.
This Policy shall be reviewed at least once every five years.

policies.name: Research and Development Policy
policies.purpose: Institutional support for faculty research, development and sabbatical leaves, and encouragement to secure outside funding.

provisions.text: The Committee on Faculty Research and Development, comprising senior faculty of the institute, reviews and administers policies of institutional support for faculty research, development and sabbatical leaves, and encourages and assists faculty in securing outside funding. Its powers, duties and functions are: making decisions concerning load reductions and technology grants, reported to and effective on management approval; encouraging faculty to write proposals and seek grants from external sources like CSIR, UGC, AICTE, DST and DAE; recommending support needed by faculty to the Principal; preparing projected and revised budgets for research; formulating recommendations and policy for the strategic development of research and research training; monitoring operational goals within the Institute's Strategic Plan and enhancing the quality of research performance and environment; and advising the Principal and management on national and international trends and the appropriate use of funds allocated to research.

The Research Committee generally meets once a month in person or by conference telephone or other communications equipment by which all participants can hear each other, with additional meetings as deemed necessary. The Research Committee submits feedback concerning research and development to the management regularly.

Every research proposal shall pass through a multi-tier review: first reviewed by the PI and Co-PI themselves, then by the concerned Head, experts or mentors in the department, followed by other eminent researchers in the field; the proposal is then vetted by the Research Review Committee (RRC) before submission to the funding agency. All applications related to R&D shall be routed through the Dean R&D along with one hard copy for R&D records; a soft copy shall also be emailed to the Dean R&D, with the department representative in the R&D cell and the HOD copied.

If the Principal Investigator leaves the institute, all items, instruments and software purchased shall remain an asset of the institute, and the Co-PI shall be fully responsible for completing the project as per the guidelines of the concerned apex bodies.

All Principal Investigators of funded and non-funded projects shall submit a half yearly report to the Dean R&D through the concerned HOD. After completion of the project, one copy of the final report shall also be submitted to the Dean R&D.

provisions.section: 12.5.9 Policy for Procurement and Maintenance item 1
provisions.text: The purchase committee for any research project comprises the Principal, Dean R&D, the concerned HOD and the PI/Co-PI. Their role is to streamline purchase requests and gauge their utility in completion of the project. The committee also looks into the recruitment of JRF/SRF, if any.

The PI shall settle the accounts for the released amount on or before 31st of March every year. The entire purchase of equipment for a research project shall be completed positively within one month of receiving the grant from the management or funding agencies. A minimum of three quotations are necessary for equipment to be purchased, the only exception being proprietary items for which the PI must submit a justification.

numbers.of: deadline to complete equipment purchase after receiving a grant

provisions.text: Seed money for an R&D project is distributed by the following procedure: submission of the proposal to the funding agency; application for seed money through the respective HOD; scrutiny by the R&D cell and/or RRC on sanction of the submitted project; and 25% of the sanctioned project cost is given as seed money from the department R&D budget to start procurement, which is recovered at a later stage after receiving the grant. For non-funded projects, proposals are submitted to the Principal through the respective HOD and Dean R&D, and scrutiny and sanction of the amount is done by the Research Review Committee.

numbers.of: share of sanctioned project cost given as seed money

provisions.text: The Research Review Committee (RRC) oversees research proposals by faculty and students. It comprises the Principal as chairman, the Research Promotion Officer (SVV), the Dean R&D, a Research Advisory Committee member for the concerned subject, the Head of the concerned Department, and a Subject Expert or Mentor. All prospective Principal Investigators must ensure the research proposal is presented before the RRC well in advance prior to submission; the research proposal of a faculty member shall be submitted to the funding agency ONLY after presentation to the RRC. The RRC also looks into collaboration with research organizations, MoUs with industries and overseas universities, training and consultancy, continuing education including add-on modules, and industry sponsored projects.

policies.name: Faculty Development Grants Policy
policies.purpose: Financial support for faculty participating in Faculty Development Programmes, STTPs, paper presentations, workshops, seminars and training programmes.

provisions.text: Every faculty member can get a faculty development grant of up to Rs. 15,000 per academic year for participating in Faculty Development Programmes like STTPs, paper presentations, workshops, seminars and training programmes. For availing this financial support the HOD should give recommendations stating how the particular programme is useful for the faculty.

Each faculty member is eligible for a faculty development grant only once in an academic year. In the same year, a faculty member who receives a faculty development grant cannot benefit from a paid research leave for a PhD, and vice versa.

Faculty members are advised to participate in such programmes during the vacation period. Special cases will be considered on the recommendations of the Dean-Academics and the respective HOD. If the faculty member participates during a non-vacational period, On Duty leave will be sanctioned for this period.

provisions.topic: how to apply for a faculty development grant
provisions.text: Fill the application in the prescribed format indicating the benefits of the training programme and get approval from the HOD. The application is then studied by the Dean-Academics who recommends it to the Principal for approval. The applicant provides clarifications to the Principal or accounts section if needed.

After the FDP the faculty member must submit a report on the skills acquired to the respective HOD, must give a presentation to the departmental staff sharing the knowledge gained, and must maintain a record of such programmes to be provided to the HOD as and when required.
Deputation for Ph.D. is as per the Higher Education Policy of SVV 2012 (Annexure - I), which in this handbook is the Revised Higher Studies Policy of KJSIEIT.

policies.name: Consultancy Policy
policies.purpose: Rules for offering consultancy services by teachers of the Institute to industries, the service sector, government departments and national and international agencies.
policies.scope: As per University Circular No. APD/449/1 of 2012 dated 18 February 2012.

provisions.text: Consultancy and related assignments can be taken up by full time faculty. Any employee of the Institute may take up consultancy work with prior approval of the Principal. All employees undertaking consultancy are referred to as Consultants.

Consultants shall disclose to the Dean (R&D) in writing the existence of any relationship between themselves and the client funding the consultancy project or any vendor paid from project funds, in the form of involvement of immediate relatives, or any scope for potential disproportionate self-gain. The Dean (R&D) reviews such cases and decides appropriately with the advice of a committee, to ensure no actual conflict of interest exists. Consultants may not use the Institute name or their affiliation in a manner that suggests the Institute approves or disapproves of a product or service, suggests the Institute has performed research or issued findings when it has not, misleadingly states the results of Institute research, or may be interpreted as communicating the official position of the Institute on any issue of public interest.

The time spent on consultancy and related assignments shall be limited to the equivalent of 52 working days in a year, preferably at the rate of one working day per week. In addition, Consultants may be permitted to utilize on average one non-working day per week. Ordinarily permission cannot be granted for more than 5 assignments at a time, though exceptional cases may be considered provided proper time management is ensured. Assignments may be taken up provided they do not adversely impact ongoing academic, research and related activities.

The services of permanent employees of the Institute may be utilized for the execution of consultancy projects provided it does not affect their primary functions and responsibilities. Students who are willing to work on consultancy projects may be permitted as per Institute norms, provided it does not affect their academic commitments and performance; such work by students may be compensated by suitable honoraria.
provisions.ambiguity: The 'Institute norms' governing student participation and the honoraria rates are NOT SPECIFIED IN SOURCE.

provisions.text: Travel out of campus on account of consultancy activities should be undertaken with prior intimation to the Head of the Department; in the case of Heads, intimations should be sent to the Principal. Such approvals are anticipated to be given within two working days to ensure prior commitments to clients are honoured. In emergencies, prior intimation and subsequent sanction could be considered acceptable.

numbers.of: expected approval time for consultancy travel

provisions.text: The minimum charges applicable in respect of consultancy jobs will be Rs. 10,000 excluding any applicable tax. It is desirable that Preliminary Diagnostic Discussions and Site Visits leading to consultancy proposals be charged at a minimum rate of Rs. 5,000 per day or part thereof, in addition to travel and incidental expenses. The charges once finalized will not be negotiable; however if the scope is altered a fresh estimate may be considered.

numbers.of: minimum consultancy job charge, excluding tax
minimum charge for preliminary diagnostic discussions and site visits

provisions.text: In extreme emergencies a consultant may take up an assignment with intimation to the Dean (R&D) and then seek approval. It would however be necessary to ensure the task involved is not a major one, entailing total charges not more than Rs. 50,000 or two days of faculty time, and that payments are made immediately, well before submission of any formal report.

numbers.of: maximum charges for an emergency assignment taken before approval
maximum faculty time for an emergency assignment

provisions.section: 12.5.7 Rules for Costing of Consultancy Projects
provisions.text: Consultancy project costing is based on: consultant fees including charges for the time of Institute and external consultants; charges for personnel engaged in technical services, payable to permanent employees for their effort; salaries payable to temporary staff employed specifically for the project; operational expenses including consumables, contingencies, travel and daily allowance, honoraria for students and equipment utilization charges for the use of institute equipment, which are transferred to the respective Departmental Development Fund (DDF); overheads charged based on salaries and operational expenses; and capital equipment charges for the purchase of specific equipment for the project, on which no overheads are charged. Service tax and other applicable taxes are provided for in the project cost.

The Consultant should be aware of the potential for the generation of Intellectual Property during the execution of projects. The Intellectual Property Policy of the Institute will govern all decisions and actions concerning the generation, handling, protection and commercialization of Intellectual Property.

policies.name: Industry Institute Interaction and Alumni Corporate Relations Policy
policies.purpose: Bridging the gap between the academic and community world, and maintaining relations with alumni.

provisions.text: The Industry Institute Interaction Cell (IIIC) is established to bridge the gap between the academic and community world, led by the Dean - Industry Institute Interaction and comprising one faculty member from each department. Its major objectives are to sign MoUs with different industries for various academic activities; identify student project work in industries; organize a Job Fair to increase placement; arrange guest lectures and seminars of industry experts at regular intervals; organize industrial visits and training for students and faculty; and encourage students to join internship programs at various industries.
Any student who has successfully completed a Bachelor degree from KJSIEIT is eligible to be a member of the KJSIEIT Alumni Association, with a lifetime membership fee of Rs. 400.

Facilities for alumni: (1) Alumni Help desk dealing with queries related to transcripts, faculty weekly offs, availability of faculty members and Leaving Certificates; (2) Alumni Referral Program, a platform to stay in touch with classmates and alumni from different batches and explore new opportunities; (3) Alumni Mentoring Program for experienced alumni who wish to mentor young graduates, fresh pass-outs and current students; (4) Alumni Privilege Card, allowing alumni to use library facilities after graduating, including issuing books and using library space and internet facilities; (5) College Infrastructure at concessional rates - the college can provide the auditorium and college ground with prior permission from a higher authority; (6) Annual Alumni Meet, a get-together called AlumNite organized in the month of January; (7) Alumni Newsletter with information about current happenings in college and updates about batch mates.
